la:HB 1243.title: SEWERAGE/N O WATER BD: Provides relative to the Sewerage and Water Board of New Orleans
la:HB 1243.summary: Removes the state-law makeup of the New Orleans Sewerage and Water Board, including its selection committee and quorum rule, and lets the board's composition follow the city charter, with the city council setting appointment and term rules by ordinance.

la:HB 1256.title: PROPERTY/UNCLAIMED: Provides with respect to abandoned digital assets
la:HB 1256.summary: Adds digital assets to the unclaimed property law, presuming them abandoned after three years without owner contact or returned mail. Requires holders to warn owners that the asset may be liquidated if they do not respond.

la:HB 153.title: COURTS/CRIMINAL: Provides with respect to the collection of criminal court fines and fees
la:HB 153.summary: Bars reporting criminal fines and fees debt to credit bureaus or consumer reporting agencies. Does not apply to traffic law violations under Title 32 or municipal law violations. Takes effect August 1, 2026.

la:HB 210.title: ETHICS/CODE: Provides for restrictions on payments from nonpublic sources
la:HB 210.summary: Bars statewide elected officials from being paid for lobbying, consulting or advising. Applies retroactively an existing exception letting school board and local governing authority members work for employers doing business with their government, except where an ethics body has issued a final decision.

la:HB 211.title: COURTS: Provides relative to the creation, administration, and eligibility requirements of the Homelessness Court program (EN SEE FISC NOTE GF EX)
la:HB 211.summary: Lets district courts create Homelessness Court programs with probation conditions, and creates the crime of unauthorized camping on public property, punishable by up to $500, six months in jail, or both. Offenders may qualify for court programs.

la:HB 325.title: TOPS: Provides relative to TOPS-Tech (EN INCREASE GF EX See Note)
la:HB 325.summary: Lets part-time students receive TOPS awards in some cases. For TOPS-Tech, adds a third eligibility criterion of nine early college credit hours, and students qualify by meeting two of three criteria, for 2026-2027 graduates onward.

la:HB 398.title: PUBLIC OFFLS/EMPS: Prohibits payment for meals and incidental expenses for state public officials and employees from exceeding amounts for such expenses established by the U.S. General Services Administration
la:HB 398.summary: Caps reimbursement for meals and incidental expenses of judicial, legislative and executive branch officers and employees at the U.S. General Services Administration daily maximum rates, with an allowance for agency-hosted conferences and working meals.

la:HB 399.title: CRIMINAL/PROCEDURE: Provides relative to temporary release of inmates for limited purposes (EN SEE FISC NOTE GF EX)
la:HB 399.summary: Extends from 60 to 120 days the expected time of death that lets the corrections secretary grant temporary release to an inmate with a terminal illness for palliative or medical care. Takes effect August 1, 2026.

la:HB 410.title: CIVIL/PROCEDURE: Requires notification of all parties to record in-person communication
la:HB 410.summary: Bars using wearable video-recording eyeglasses to record or transcribe a conversation unless all participants are notified. Exempts public meetings, law enforcement and emergencies, recording evidence for legal proceedings, and recordings made by a participant in their own home or business.

la:HB 414.title: HEALTH: Provides for prohibitions on hiring individuals with certain criminal convictions
la:HB 414.summary: Requires background checks on anyone owning or managing a therapeutic group home, removes licensed ambulance personnel from hiring bans for criminal offenses, and lets hospitals run criminal history checks through accredited consumer reporting agencies.

la:HB 420.title: CHILDREN/DCFS: Requires the Department of Children and Family Services to obtain background checks on all employees (EN INCREASE GF EX See Note)
la:HB 420.summary: Requires the Department of Children and Family Services to run criminal background checks and state central registry searches on all current and prospective employees, not only those in child-facing roles, and extends the termination rule for registry matches.

la:HB 459.title: ELECTIONS/CANDIDATES: Provides relative to the use of artificial intelligence in political campaigns
la:HB 459.summary: Bars electioneering communications showing AI-altered images, likenesses or voices of candidates that falsely appear authentic, unless clearly labeled as AI-created. Penalties apply only when done with intent to injure a candidate's reputation or deceive voters. Exempts broadcasters with no control over content.

la:HB 481.title: PUBLIC PRINTING: Provides for the cost of publishing official proceedings and public notices
la:HB 481.summary: Raises the maximum rate parishes, municipalities and school boards may pay by contract to publish official proceedings and public notices to three cents per character in all parishes, up from two cents or one and a half cents.

la:HB 538.title: COURTS/JUVENILE: Provides relative to the judicial expense fund for the Juvenile Court for the parish of East Baton Rouge
la:HB 538.summary: Raises the maximum additional civil filing fee for the East Baton Rouge Juvenile Court judicial expense fund from $15 to $45 and gives the judges sitting together, rather than the chief judge, control of the fee and fund.

la:HB 593.title: MTR VEHICLE/OFFICE: Increases the maximum service and transaction fee a governing authority may assess to fund an office of motor vehicles field office not fully funded by the state (EN +$1,540,000 LF RV See Note)
la:HB 593.summary: Raises the maximum local fee per transaction at Office of Motor Vehicles field offices to $8 statewide, up from $4.50 and higher caps in a few places, with Shreveport field offices exempt. Takes effect August 1, 2026.

la:HB 608.title: ATHLETICS: Provides relative to the confidentiality of documents related to an intercollegiate athletics revenue sharing program
la:HB 608.summary: Makes the total revenue a college spends on athlete revenue sharing public, but keeps confidential each athlete's payment, each sport's allocation, and negotiation records. Applies to past and pending records requests.

la:HB 690.title: EDUCATION: Provides relative to education service providers and vendors of educational products (EN NO IMPACT   See Note)
la:HB 690.summary: Bars education agencies from knowingly contracting with education service providers or vendors that are foreign adversaries, foreign terrorist organizations or their agents, and bars subcontracting with them. Requires notifying the attorney general and suspending payments pending review.

la:HB 719.title: DISTRICT ATTORNEYS/ASST: Provides relative to the number of assistant district attorneys in each judicial district (EN +$3,411,000 GF EX See Note)
la:HB 719.summary: Raises the number of assistant district attorneys authorized in most judicial districts, for example from 55 to 71 in the 19th and from 30 to 44 in the 22nd, and leaves several districts unchanged.

la:HB 723.title: MTR VEHICLE/MOTORCYCLES: Authorizes drivers of certain two-wheeled vehicles to proceed through a red light under certain circumstances
la:HB 723.summary: Lets drivers of motorcycles, mopeds and bicycles proceed through a red light at a vehicle-actuated signal after stopping for two full cycles or two minutes, treating it as a stop sign, and yielding to pedestrians and cross traffic.

la:HB 730.title: AIRCRAFT/AVIATION: Provides relative to the use of automatic dependent surveillance-broadcast systems (EN SEE FISC NOTE LF RV)
la:HB 730.summary: Bars using aircraft tracking data from ADS-B systems as a basis for charging fees or taxes to owners of aircraft of 12,499 pounds or less operating in the state.

la:HB 732.title: MTR VEHICLE/OFFICE: Provides for a temporary waiver of fees for final delinquent debt based on special circumstances (EN DECREASE SG RV See Note)
la:HB 732.summary: Lets the motor vehicles commissioner pause fines, fees and license suspensions for up to 30 days so a person can get life-sustaining medicine or treatment. Suspends the road usage fee on non-plug-in hybrids until August 1, 2027.

la:HB 75.title: GAMING: Creates an enhanced promotional play pilot program relative to net slot machine proceeds (EN -$574,627 GF RV See Note)
la:HB 75.summary: Creates a pilot program, July 2026 through June 2027, raising the promotional play wagers racing-facility slot licensees may offer from $5 million to $7 million. Requires licensees to report the effect on proceeds, fees and taxes by March 1, 2027.

la:HB 750.title: CONSUMERS/PROTECTION: Provides for cancellation of automatic renewal subscriptions
la:HB 750.summary: Creates the Click-to-Cancel Act, requiring businesses with automatic renewal subscriptions to disclose terms clearly, get affirmative consent, send an acknowledgment, keep consent records for a year, and offer an easy, timely cancellation method.

la:HB 769.title: DOMESTIC ABUSE: Provides relative to the removal authority process with respect to domestic offenders
la:HB 769.summary: Lets courts hold a person charged with certain domestic abuse offenses without bail for a 48 to 72 hour cooling-off period, considering any increased risk to the victim, family or public. The period runs within the 72-hour limit for first appearance.

la:HB 775.title: HEALTH/CHILDREN: Provides relative to minor's consent for medical procedures and treatments
la:HB 775.summary: Requires parental or guardian consent before health care providers treat a person under the age of majority, replacing prior law letting minors consent. Lists exceptions, including military service, emancipation, pregnancy care, substance misuse treatment, and sexually transmitted disease treatment.

la:HB 804.title: ENERGY: Creates the Louisiana Energy Protection Act (EN NO IMPACT   See Note)
la:HB 804.summary: Bars lawsuits in Louisiana courts seeking damages for climate change from greenhouse gas emissions, except claims over violations of emission laws, permit terms or certain federal workplace safety standards.

la:HB 848.title: MTR VEHICLE/DEALERS: Provides with respect to all terrain vehicle dealerships
la:HB 848.summary: Adds golf carts to the all-terrain vehicle dealer law, covers any retailer selling them, and requires such dealers to have adequate facilities to support warranty service, maintenance and repair of the vehicles they sell.

la:HB 864.title: HIGHWAYS: Authorizes municipalities to establish fire limits and to prohibit the storage, placement, accumulation, abandonment, or use of certain materials within the right-of-way of certain public structures
la:HB 864.summary: Lets municipalities set fire limits and bar storing or using flammable, explosive or combustible material above ground in the right-of-way of public bridges, overpasses and tunnels. Violations carry fines up to $1,000, with exceptions for permitted events and utilities.

la:HB 951.title: LABOR: Creates the office of business workforce solutions within Louisiana Works (EN INCREASE GF EX See Note)
la:HB 951.summary: Creates the office of business workforce solutions within Louisiana Works, adds duties for the Workforce Investment Council, and treats employer outreach spending for the Incumbent Worker Training Program as non-administrative expense.

la:HB 953.title: PLUMBERS: Provides relative to plumbing licenses
la:HB 953.summary: Abolishes the State Plumbing Board and moves plumber and gas fitter licensing to a new Plumbing Contractors Subcommittee of the State Licensing Board for Contractors, adding two board members from plumbing industry groups.

la:HB 956.title: FIRE PROTECT/FIRE MARSHAL: Provides relative to fireworks
la:HB 956.summary: Changes fireworks rules: limits retail sales to 1.4G-class fireworks, starts sale hours at 7 a.m., adds Memorial Day and Labor Day sale windows, repeals Class C public displays, and raises pyrotechnic operator license fees to $200 new and $100 renewal.

la:HB 971.title: MEDICAID: Provides relative to Medicaid reimbursement for rural health clinics (EN +$2,655,159 GF EX See Note)
la:HB 971.summary: Requires the Department of Health to equalize Medicaid rates between independent and provider-based rural health clinics, raising the independent clinic encounter rate subject to federal approval. Adds rural health clinics to facility need review and requires monthly encounter and spending reports.

la:HB 989.title: MOTOR VEHICLES: Modifies charges collected by public license tag agents
la:HB 989.summary: Raises the maximum convenience charge and the registration reinstatement fee that public license tag agents may collect from $23 to $27.

la:SB 237.title: CHILDREN: Provides relative to child welfare. (8/1/26) (EN NO IMPACT   See Note)
la:SB 237.summary: Changes child welfare notification and oversight: requires notice of child abuse deaths to legislative leaders and committee chairs, requires reporting of deaths and near-fatalities to the child ombudsman, and gives the ombudsman remote access to state child-services systems.

la:SB 268.title: LOCAL FINANCE: Provides for lead service line replacement. (8/1/26)
la:SB 268.summary: Lets municipalities adopt ordinances allowing city water systems to enter private property to replace lead service lines after at least seven days' notice, except in emergencies. Entry is limited to the replacement work.

la:SB 283.title: SPECIAL DISTRICTS: Creates the BLVD at Harding Area Special District in the city of Baton Rouge. (gov sig)
la:SB 283.summary: Creates two special districts in Baton Rouge, the BLVD at Harding Area district and a Baton Rouge Community College economic development district, each run by a board with power to issue bonds. Extends tax increment financing authority to the Harding district.

la:SB 384.title: TECHNOLOGY: Authorizes creation of the Pilot Innovation Hub. (8/1/26) (EN SEE FISC NOTE LF EX See Note)
la:SB 384.summary: Lets parishes designate themselves Pilot Innovation Hubs, where local governments may contract with a pilot innovation contractor to test new technologies, using public property and aligned permitting and zoning.

la:SB 387.title: HEALTH/ACC INSURANCE: Provides relative to pharmacy benefit managers. (1/1/27) (EN INCREASE SG EX See Note)
la:SB 387.summary: Regulates pharmacy benefit managers: limits their pay to flat fees, bars keeping rebates and spread pricing, and allows annual audits. Sets a $25,000 civil penalty per violation, with license suspension or revocation if not corrected within 30 days.

la:SB 406.title: TAX/LOCAL: Authorizes the city of Slidell to levy a hotel occupancy tax. (gov sig) (EN +$590,000 LF RV See Note)
la:SB 406.summary: Lets the city of Slidell, with voter approval, levy a hotel occupancy tax of up to 2% of room charges, with proceeds funding recreational facilities or tourism initiatives named in the tax proposition.

la:SB 433.title: MEDICAID: Provides for Medicaid coverage of certain medications. (1/1/27) (EN +$3,000,000 GF EX See Note)
la:SB 433.summary: Requires Medicaid to cover medically necessary, FDA-approved weight loss medications for recipients who meet Department of Health criteria. Allows prior authorization, bars step therapy, and takes effect upon legislative appropriation.

la:SB 444.title: EXPROPRIATION: Provides relative to expropriation by the city of St. George. (gov sig)
la:SB 444.summary: Lets the city of St. George take property by expropriation for public projects such as streets, drainage, utilities and flood protection, using the same procedures as the Department of Transportation and Development, including taking before judgment.

la:SB 449.title: PUBLIC CONTRACTS: Provides for the procurement of materials and goods. (8/1/26)
la:SB 449.summary: Exempts political subdivisions that own or operate a railroad from public bid requirements when buying used locomotives, rolling stock, track maintenance equipment and their parts. Takes effect August 1, 2026.

la:SB 479.title: JUDGES: Provides for legislative address to the governor for the removal of certain judges for malfeasance, gross misconduct, or incompetence committed while in office. (See Act)
la:SB 479.summary: Sets procedures for impeaching state officials and judges, including a defined "gross misconduct" standard, sworn citizen complaints, and a joint legislative investigating committee with subpoena power. Lets the House impeach by majority vote.

la:SB 513.title: PUBLIC CONTRACTS: Provides for public works project delivery methods. (8/1/26)
la:SB 513.summary: Lets public airports use design-build contracting for vertical facilities such as workforce training buildings, control towers, parking garages and hangars, excluding commercial airport passenger terminals and equipment. Takes effect August 1, 2026.

md:HB 1118.title: Health, Health Insurance, and Health Occupations - Perinatal Behavioral Health Conditions
md:HB 1118.summary: Requires Medicaid and insurers, from January 1, 2027, to cover screening for perinatal behavioral health conditions such as postpartum depression. Requires providers to screen at well visits in a child's first year and the health department to identify screening tools.

md:HB 1137.title: Residential-in-Commercial-Zone Laws - Study (Bring Back Main Street Act)
md:HB 1137.summary: Requires the Department of Housing and Community Development to study laws requiring local governments to allow residential or mixed-use development on commercially zoned lots, and report by December 1, 2026.

md:HB 1151.title: Maryland Department of Health - Study on Maryland Medical Assistance Program Reimbursement of Hospice Room and Board Services
md:HB 1151.summary: Requires the Health Care Commission and Medicaid to study the effects of Medicaid paying for hospice house room and board, including costs, savings and hospital use, with a report to legislative committees by December 1, 2026.

md:HB 1216.title: Insurance – Certificates of Guarantee for County Bond Requirements – All Counties
md:HB 1216.summary: Lets all counties, not only some, accept certificates of guarantee from certain associations or contractors to meet county bond requirements.

md:HB 1243.title: Prince George's County - Personal Property Tax Exemption for Small Manufacturers PG 423-26
md:HB 1243.summary: Exempts personal property of small manufacturers holding an alcoholic beverages manufacturer's license, with 50 or fewer employees, from municipal personal property tax in Prince George's County, for tax years beginning after June 30, 2026.

md:HB 1286.title: Anne Arundel County - Alcoholic Beverages - Barbershop and Beauty Salon License
md:HB 1286.summary: Lets Anne Arundel County barbershop and beauty salon license holders serve each customer up to 1.7 ounces of liquor per visit for on-premises consumption, in addition to beer and wine.

md:HB 1300.title: African American Heritage Preservation Program and Maryland Commission for Women - Renaming and Alterations
md:HB 1300.summary: Renames the African American Heritage Preservation Program for Speaker Adrienne A. Jones, makes the Maryland Commission for Women's executive director a skilled service state employee rather than a Secretary appointee, and changes the commission's duties.

md:HB 1321.title: Child Care Scholarship Program - Application Process and Copays - Alterations
md:HB 1321.summary: Requires the State Department of Education to help Child Care Scholarship applicants who qualify for public prekindergarten or Head Start enroll in those programs while a waitlist exists, and limits certain copays.

md:HB 1335.title: Department of Information Technology - Information Technology Staffing and Capability Assessment - Independent Study
md:HB 1335.summary: Requires the Department of Information Technology to hire an outside party to study IT and cybersecurity staffing and workforce alignment in the State, and submit the study by November 1, 2027.

md:HB 1430.title: Maryland Public Charter School Program - School Facilities - Funding
md:HB 1430.summary: Requires the Governor, from fiscal 2028, to budget capital improvement funds for public charter school facilities equal to prior-year charter enrollment times $200, distributed directly to schools by the Interagency Commission on School Construction.

md:HB 1434.title: Maryland Department of Health - Caregiver Resource Webpage - Establishment
md:HB 1434.summary: Requires the Maryland Department of Health to create and maintain a webpage of information and resources for caregivers.

md:HB 1466.title: Department of Housing and Community Development - Appraisal Gap From Historic Redlining Financial Assistance Program - Qualified Properties
md:HB 1466.summary: Expands the definition of a qualified property under the Appraisal Gap From Historic Redlining Financial Assistance Program.

md:HB 1470.title: Medical Assistance Programs - Drug Dispensing - Cost-of-Dispensing Survey
md:HB 1470.summary: Requires the Maryland Department of Health to conduct its in-State drug cost-of-dispensing survey for Medicaid at least every 3 years, starting in 2026, and report results to the General Assembly by December 1 of survey years.

md:HB 1490.title: Family Investment Program - Temporary Cash Assistance - Good Cause and Adequate Reason Exceptions
md:HB 1490.summary: Bars the Department of Human Services from denying or cutting temporary cash assistance when a person has good cause for not cooperating with child support, and defines good cause as cooperation possibly harming the child.

md:HB 1587.title: Gaming - Operation of Electronic Instant Bingo Machines and Report by State Lottery and Gaming Control Agency
md:HB 1587.summary: Raises from 54 to 100 the bingo cards a handheld device may play at once under the slot machine definition, lets electronic instant bingo machines skip paper tickets unless the player asks, and requires a state report on expanding them by December 1, 2026.

md:HB 161.title: Property Tax Credit - Retail Service Station Conversions
md:HB 161.summary: Lets Baltimore City and counties or municipalities grant a property tax credit on land converted from a retail gas station to other uses, only if underground storage tanks have been permanently closed.

md:HB 191.title: Consumer Protection - Retail Transactions for Essential Consumer Goods - Cash Payments
md:HB 191.summary: Bars merchants from refusing cash, requiring cards, or charging cash payers more for essential goods such as food, medicine and fuel in in-person sales under $300 between 6 a.m. and 10 p.m. Violations count as unfair or deceptive trade practices.

md:HB 200.title: Sale of Residential Real Property - Required Flood Risk Disclosure
md:HB 200.summary: Requires the Department of the Environment to create a flood risk disclosure form, and from July 1, 2027 requires sellers of certain homes to give buyers a completed form before signing a sale contract.

md:HB 2100.title: Election Districts - General Assembly and Representatives in Congress
md:HB 2100.summary: Proposes a constitutional amendment, for the November 2026 ballot, stating that the state constitution provides no criteria for congressional district boundaries, limits legislative district requirements to state House and Senate districts, and lets the legislature give the Supreme Court original jurisdiction over congressional maps.

md:HB 2101.title: Arbitration Reform for State Employees Act of 2026 - Withdraw and Repeal of Duplicate Proposed Constitutional Amendment
md:HB 2101.summary: Repeals a duplicate proposed constitutional amendment on collective bargaining for State employees, so only one copy appears on the November 2026 ballot. An identical amendment in another act stays on the ballot. Takes effect immediately as an emergency.

md:HB 211.title: Baltimore County – Property Tax Credit – Fraternal Order of Police Lodge 34
md:HB 211.summary: Lets Baltimore County grant a property tax credit on certain real property owned by Fraternal Order of Police Lodge 34, for tax years after June 30, 2026.

md:HB 306.title: Vehicle Laws - Manufacturers and Dealers - Prices Listed on Dealer Websites (Jack Fitzgerald Price Transparency Act)
md:HB 306.summary: Bars vehicle manufacturers from penalizing a dealer for stating on its website that an advertised price is the manufacturer's minimum advertised price and that the dealer may offer a lower price.

md:HB 315.title: Landlord and Tenant - Discrimination in Housing for Income-Based Housing Subsidies and Positive Rental History Reporting
md:HB 315.summary: Bars landlords from refusing to rent to prospective tenants who use income-based housing subsidies, and from using credit history from before the subsidy, with exceptions. Violations are discriminatory housing practices. Requires offering to report tenants' positive rent payment history.

md:HB 326.title: Education - Maryland Center for School Safety - Anonymous Reporting System
md:HB 326.summary: Requires the Maryland Center for School Safety to run an anonymous system for reporting school or student safety concerns, and requires each local school system to participate, with reports kept from public inspection.

md:HB 330.title: Maryland Legal Services Corporation - Board of Directors - Membership
md:HB 330.summary: Increases the Maryland Legal Services Corporation Board of Directors from 9 to 12 members.

md:HB 396.title: Residential Child Care Programs - Education of Children and Training of Child and Youth Care Practitioners
md:HB 396.summary: Requires residential child care programs to keep children age 5 and older enrolled in their prior school unless a social services department decides otherwise, and sets requirements for approved training programs for residential child and youth care practitioners. Takes effect January 1, 2027.

md:HB 457.title: Institutions of Higher Education - Provision of Menstrual Hygiene Products - Requirement
md:HB 457.summary: Requires colleges that offer on-campus housing to provide free menstrual hygiene products in all student health centers by August 1, 2028.

md:HB 497.title: Family Law - Temporary and Final Protective Orders - Duration
md:HB 497.summary: Lengthens temporary protective orders from up to 7 days after service to up to 14 days after issuance, and requires the final protective order hearing within 14 days after the temporary order is issued.

md:HB 529.title: Code Revision - Health - Maryland Medical Assistance Program
md:HB 529.summary: Revises, restates and recodifies the State's laws on the Maryland Medical Assistance Program.

md:HB 548.title: Land Use - Permitting - Development Rights (Maryland Housing Certainty Act)
md:HB 548.summary: Requires local governments to judge housing development applications under the laws in effect when a complete application is submitted, decide completeness within 30 days, and gives approved projects vested development rights for the longer of five years or a locally set period.

md:HB 552.title: Commission on the House of Reformation and Instruction for Colored Children - Establishment
md:HB 552.summary: Creates the Commission on the House of Reformation and Instruction for Colored Children to direct an investigation of the historic site, including locating graves, identifying people buried there, notifying descendants, and a final report by December 31, 2029.

md:HB 561.title: Maryland Child Care Credential Program - Extension of Funding
md:HB 561.summary: Requires the Governor to appropriate $5,687,000 to the Maryland Child Care Credential Program in each of fiscal years 2028 through 2030.

md:HB 571.title: Nonprofit Housing Corporations - Taxes and Special Assessments Exemptions - Alterations
md:HB 571.summary: Broadens the definition of nonprofit housing corporation for property tax and special assessment exemptions and extends the exemption to certain subsidiaries, except for property in Baltimore City.

md:HB 573.title: Fair Housing and Housing Discrimination - Regulations, Intent, and Discriminatory Effect
md:HB 573.summary: Bars housing practices that have a discriminatory effect, meaning a disparate impact on protected groups or reinforcing segregated housing patterns, even without intent. Authorizes the housing department to adopt regulations on affirmatively furthering fair housing.

md:HB 586.title: County Boards of Library Trustees - Membership - Student Member
md:HB 586.summary: Lets a county library board of trustees choose a student member, and sets qualifications, a one-year term and voting rights for that member.

md:HB 6.title: Public Institutions of Higher Education - Pregnant and Parenting Students - Plan and Reporting
md:HB 6.summary: Requires the Higher Education Commission to collect data on students' parental status from public colleges and universities, requires community colleges to adopt a plan for pregnant and parenting students, and requires a report to the legislature by September 1, 2027.

md:HB 680.title: Children's Cabinet Fund - Renaming and Funding for Grants to Local Management Boards
md:HB 680.summary: Renames the Children's Cabinet Fund the Children's Cabinet Interagency Fund and requires budget appropriations to it for fiscal years 2028-2030 at least equal to 2027's, then $500,000 more in 2031, for grants to local management boards.

md:HB 684.title: Health Insurance - Material Changes to Provider Networks - Notification and Special Enrollment Period
md:HB 684.summary: Changes notice requirements for health insurers and health systems about contract terminations and provider network changes, requiring notice to enrollees and the Insurance Commissioner.

md:HB 711.title: Data Privacy - Consumer Data, Public Records, and Message Switching System (Data Privacy Act)
md:HB 711.summary: Bars data controllers from knowingly selling consumers' personal data to government units that have engaged in or supported civil immigration enforcement, and requires public record custodians and message switching system operators to take steps related to immigration-enforcement access.

md:HB 742.title: Growing Family Child Care Opportunities Program - Funding
md:HB 742.summary: Requires the Governor to include $450,000 in the annual budget for the Growing Family Child Care Opportunities Program in fiscal years 2028 through 2030.

md:HB 805.title: Building Homes Act
md:HB 805.summary: Lets Baltimore City and counties or municipalities grant a property tax credit on homes with nonprofit-provided mortgages and covenants that keep the price affordable, for tax years after June 30, 2026.

md:HB 811.title: Aging-in-Place Programs - Grants - Multigenerational Third Places ( Village Multigenerational Third Places Act)
md:HB 811.summary: Lets the Department of Aging give grants to nonprofits and area agencies on aging to support social connection for aging-in-place participants through events at multigenerational third places, meaning community spaces used by people of different ages.

md:HB 816.title: Maryland Automobile Insurance Fund - Affordability Program and Industry Automobile Insurance Association Assessments
md:HB 816.summary: Changes the cap on an insurer assessment allocation percentage for the Industry Automobile Insurance Association and lets the Maryland Automobile Insurance Fund's director set up an affordability program.

md:HB 849.title: Child Care Scholarship Program - Freeze in Enrollment - Exceptions and Waitlist
md:HB 849.summary: Bars Child Care Scholarship enrollment freezes from covering certain groups such as children with enrolled siblings and homeless children, and requires a waitlist with priority enrollment for certain applicants.

md:HB 862.title: Railroads - Required Crew for Movement of Freight
md:HB 862.summary: Bars freight trains from operating in Maryland with fewer than two crew members, with exceptions, and sets fines of up to $10,000, or up to $25,000 for a willful violation within 3 years of a prior one.

md:HB 866.title: Workgroup for the Deaf, Deafblind, and Hard of Hearing - Extension
md:HB 866.summary: Extends the Workgroup for the Deaf, Deafblind, and Hard of Hearing to December 31, 2028, and moves its report deadline to December 1, 2028.

md:HB 894.title: Land Use - Transit-Oriented Development - Alterations (Maryland Transit and Housing Opportunity Act)
md:HB 894.summary: Makes new transit-oriented developments near frequent rail service enterprise zones unless the local government opts out, prioritizes land near rail stations for state infrastructure loans, and bars local minimum parking requirements and some land use limits near stations.

md:HB 919.title: Maryland Higher Education Commission - Practical Applications of Real Estate Appraisal (PAREA) Grant Program - Established
md:HB 919.summary: Creates a grant program, run by the Maryland Higher Education Commission, to help people become real estate appraisers in historically redlined and underrepresented communities.

md:SB 16.title: Child Support - Earnings Withholdings Limits
md:SB 16.summary: Caps child support earnings withholding at 35% of disposable earnings for obligors whose income is at or below 250% of the federal poverty level for one person, and lets employees contest withholding amounts.

md:SB 168.title: Study to Evaluate Blockchain-Based Real Property Lease and Title Recordation and Verification
md:SB 168.summary: Requires the State Department of Assessments and Taxation to study using blockchain to record and verify property ownership and leases, including for squatting disputes, and report by December 31, 2026.

md:SB 169.title: Hospitals - Emergency Pregnancy-Related Medical Conditions - Procedures
md:SB 169.summary: Requires hospitals to screen emergency department patients for emergency pregnancy-related conditions, sets rules for their treatment and transfer, and requires hospitals to allow pregnancy termination in certain circumstances.

md:SB 198.title: Prince George's Community College - Aerospace and Aviation Systems Technology Programs - Feasibility Study
md:SB 198.summary: Requires Prince George's Community College to study aerospace and aviation systems technology training programs and report to the General Assembly by December 1, 2027, with $100,000 in the 2028 budget for the study.

md:SB 244.title: Code Revision - Health - Maryland Medical Assistance Program
md:SB 244.summary: Revises, restates and recodifies the State's laws on the Maryland Medical Assistance Program.

md:SB 252.title: Maryland Legal Services Corporation - Board of Directors - Membership
md:SB 252.summary: Increases the Maryland Legal Services Corporation Board of Directors from 9 to 12 members.

md:SB 253.title: Baltimore County Public Library - Collective Bargaining - Supervisory Employees
md:SB 253.summary: Lets supervisory employees of the Baltimore County Public Library form or join employee organizations and bargain collectively, and authorizes bargaining units for library employees.

md:SB 276.title: Maryland Medical Assistance Program and Health Insurance - Coverage for Orthoses and Prostheses (So Every Body Can Move Act)
md:SB 276.summary: Requires Medicaid and certain insurers to cover orthoses starting January 1, 2027, and clarifies that required prosthesis coverage includes all prostheses a provider finds medically necessary for daily living, work or physical activities.

md:SB 30.title: Baltimore County - Property Tax Credit - Fraternal Order of Police Lodge 34
md:SB 30.summary: Lets Baltimore County grant a 100% county property tax credit on certain real property owned by Fraternal Order of Police Lodge 34, for tax years after June 30, 2026.

md:SB 322.title: Courts - Jury Service - Disqualification
md:SB 322.summary: Changes jury disqualification: a person convicted of a crime punishable by over a year is disqualified while serving the sentence, including parole or probation. Also disqualifies those convicted of perjury, witness or jury intimidation, or fraud crimes. Repeals the pardon provision.

md:SB 324.title: Higher Education - Public Senior Higher Education Institutions - Direct Admission Program and Study
md:SB 324.summary: Creates a direct admission program at participating public senior colleges starting 2028-2029, offering conditional admission with a waived application fee to high school students who meet set requirements, including college and career ready standards and a minimum GPA.

md:SB 325.title: Land Use - Permitting - Development Rights (Maryland Housing Certainty Act)
md:SB 325.summary: Requires housing development applications to be judged only under laws in effect when a complete application is submitted, and gives approved projects vested development rights for 5 years or a locally set period, whichever is longer.

md:SB 366.title: Motor Vehicles - Intelligent Speed Assistance System Pilot Program - Establishment
md:SB 366.summary: Creates a pilot program requiring people facing certain driver's license suspensions or revocations to get a restricted license and use an aftermarket intelligent speed assistance device that prevents the vehicle from exceeding the speed limit.

md:SB 379.title: Recovery Residence Grant Program - Funding
md:SB 379.summary: Extends through fiscal year 2030 the requirement to include $500,000 in the state budget for the Recovery Residence Grant Program.

md:SB 401.title: Anne Arundel County - Board of License Commissioners and Part-Time Inspectors - Compensation
md:SB 401.summary: Raises annual salaries for the chair, part-time inspectors and other members of the Anne Arundel County Board of License Commissioners and includes cost-of-living increases given to nonrepresented county employees.

md:SB 410.title: Public Libraries - State Library Resource Center - Funding
md:SB 410.summary: Changes how State Library Resource Center funding is calculated, starting in fiscal year 2028.

md:SB 414.title: Anne Arundel County - Alcoholic Beverages - Consumption-Only Nonprofit Swim Club License
md:SB 414.summary: Creates a $100 annual consumption-only license for nonprofit swim clubs in Anne Arundel County, letting members and guests bring their own alcohol to designated events, up to five days a year between 2 p.m. and 10 p.m.

md:SB 450.title: Carroll County - Office of Permits and Inspections - Denial of Commercial Permit or License for Unpaid Personal Property Taxes
md:SB 450.summary: Lets the Carroll County Office of Permits and Inspections deny or refuse to renew a commercial license or permit for unpaid personal property taxes, unless the applicant disputes the amount, and allows issuance once the taxes are shown to be paid.

md:SB 459.title: Procurement - Advertising - Maryland News Organizations (Local News for Maryland Communities Act of 2026)
md:SB 459.summary: Requires state agencies to direct at least 50% of their advertising contract dollars to Maryland news organizations, prioritizing those serving underserved communities, and allows consulting a nonprofit to keep a list of eligible local news organizations.

md:SB 461.title: Supplemental Nutrition Assistance Program - Heat and Eat Program - Study
md:SB 461.summary: Requires the Department of Human Services to study how many households lose automatic utility allowance eligibility in the SNAP Heat and Eat program under the 2025 federal budget law, and report findings and recommendations by December 1, 2026.

md:SB 467.title: Maryland Child Care Credential Program - Extension of Funding
md:SB 467.summary: Requires the Governor to include $5,687,000 a year in the budget for the Maryland Child Care Credential Program in fiscal years 2028 through 2030.

md:SB 469.title: Maryland Automobile Insurance Fund - Affordability Program and Industry Automobile Insurance Association Assessments
md:SB 469.summary: Lowers from 3% to 1% the cap on an insurer assessment allocation percentage for the Industry Automobile Insurance Association, and lets the Maryland Automobile Insurance Fund's director set up an affordability program.

md:SB 496.title: Maryland Medical Assistance Program - Coverage for the Treatment of Obesity - Authorization
md:SB 496.summary: Allows the Maryland Medical Assistance Program to cover treatment of obesity starting January 1, 2027, and lets the Health Department seek federal approval for that coverage.

md:SB 497.title: Property Tax - City of Hagerstown and the Hagerstown Multi-Use Sports and Events Facility, Inc. - Exemption
md:SB 497.summary: Exempts property owned by the City of Hagerstown and used for public social, recreational and entertainment purposes from property tax, retroactive to fiscal year 2024, with refunds of excess tax paid.

md:SB 521.title: Health Insurance - Material Changes to Provider Networks - Notification and Special Enrollment Period
md:SB 521.summary: Changes notice requirements for health insurers and health systems about contract terminations and provider network changes, requiring notice to enrollees and the Insurance Commissioner.

md:SB 530.title: Aging-in-Place Programs - Grants - Multigenerational Third Places (Village Multigenerational Third Places Act)
md:SB 530.summary: Lets the Department of Aging give grants to nonprofits and area agencies on aging for events at multigenerational third places that support social connection among people in aging-in-place programs.

md:SB 532.title: Higher Education Institutions - Over-the-Counter Contraception - Access and Reporting
md:SB 532.summary: Requires public colleges and community colleges to report annually on contraception access, and requires community colleges to give students access to all over-the-counter contraception methods.

md:SB 535.title: County Boards of Library Trustees - Membership - Student Member
md:SB 535.summary: Lets a county library board of trustees choose a student member, and sets qualifications, a one-year term and voting rights for that member.

md:SB 58.title: Property Tax Credit - Retail Service Station Conversions
md:SB 58.summary: Lets Baltimore City and counties or municipalities grant a property tax credit on land converted from a retail gas station to other uses, only if underground storage tanks have been permanently closed.

md:SB 597.title: Higher Education - Maryland Artificial Intelligence Partnership
md:SB 597.summary: Creates the Maryland Artificial Intelligence Partnership within the University System of Maryland to coordinate AI workforce, business and research efforts, with a strategic plan due December 1, 2026. Also creates an AI public services fellowship and, conditionally, an AI incubation lab.

md:SB 6.title: State Personnel - Collective Bargaining - Nontenure Track Faculty
md:SB 6.summary: Gives collective bargaining rights to nontenure-track faculty at University System of Maryland institutions, Morgan State University and St. Mary's College, and creates a separate bargaining unit for them.

md:SB 637.title: Maryland Automobile Insurance Fund - Fund Producer Commission Rate
md:SB 637.summary: Lowers the minimum commission the Maryland Automobile Insurance Fund pays producers on private passenger auto policies from 10% to 5% of premium, and bars commissions on policies the Fund writes directly.

md:SB 657.title: Maryland Higher Education Commission - Practical Applications of Real Estate Appraisal (PAREA) Grant Program - Established
md:SB 657.summary: Creates a Higher Education Commission grant program for minority residents of historically redlined and underrepresented communities to complete Practical Applications of Real Estate Appraisal (PAREA) training, aimed at closing appraisal gaps and diversifying the appraisal field.

md:SB 668.title: Children's Cabinet Fund - Renaming and Funding for Grants to Local Management Boards
md:SB 668.summary: Renames the Children's Cabinet Fund the Children's Cabinet Interagency Fund and requires budget appropriations to it for fiscal years 2028-2030 at least equal to 2027's, then $500,000 more in 2031, for grants to local management boards.

md:SB 729.title: Real Property - Access to Counsel in Evictions Program - Expansion
md:SB 729.summary: Extends the Access to Counsel in Evictions Program to residents of mobile home parks, giving them legal representation in repossession actions and requiring outreach, an informational pamphlet and annual reporting that cover them.

md:SB 739.title: Climate Change, Homeowner's Insurance, and Emergency Management - Study
md:SB 739.summary: Requires the University System of Maryland to study how climate change affects homeowner's insurance availability and cost and emergency preparedness, and report recommendations to the General Assembly by July 1, 2027, including on flood insurance programs.

md:SB 747.title: Condominiums - Unit Owner Responsibility for Damage or Destruction and Mandatory Insurance Coverage
md:SB 747.summary: Makes certain condominium unit owners responsible for repair or replacement costs for damage under set conditions, requires councils of unit owners to notify owners annually, and requires unit owners to carry a unit owner insurance policy.

md:SB 769.title: University System of Maryland - Academic Facilities Bonding Authority
md:SB 769.summary: Approves academic facilities projects for the University System of Maryland and authorizes it to issue bonds to finance them, which are not debts of the State.

md:SB 791.title: Correctional Services and Criminal Procedure - Immigration Enforcement - Prohibitions (Community Trust Act)
md:SB 791.summary: Bars local jails from holding people over immigration status or federal requests without a judicial warrant, asking about status, or notifying federal authorities of custody, with exceptions. Limits police sharing information with immigration authorities without a court order.

md:SB 852.title: Anne Arundel County – Alcoholic Beverages – Barbershop and Beauty Salon License
md:SB 852.summary: Lets Anne Arundel County barbershop and beauty salon license holders serve each customer up to 1.7 ounces of liquor per visit for on-premises consumption, in addition to beer and wine.

md:SB 864.title: Higher Education - Tuition Exemption for Foster Care Recipients - Eligibility
md:SB 864.summary: Lowers from 13 to 8 the age on or after which a person must have lived in an out-of-home placement to qualify for the foster care tuition and mandatory fee exemption at public colleges. Takes effect July 1, 2026.

md:SB 865.title: Workgroup on the Affordability of Private Passenger Automobile Insurance – Extension and Alteration of Membership and Duties
md:SB 865.summary: Extends the auto insurance affordability workgroup to June 30, 2027, changes its membership, and adds duties to develop specific recommendations to reduce premiums, including on territorial rating. Requires an updated report by January 1, 2027.

md:SB 941.title: Safe and Healthy Homes for All Act
md:SB 941.summary: Requires the housing department's landlord and tenant office to develop a plan, due August 31, 2027, to identify rental properties with 50 or more units that pose severe health and safety risks and propose interventions, and to publish a list of those properties online.

mi:HB 4011.title: Property: conveyance of state property; transfer of certain state-owned property in Arenac County; provide for. Creates land transfer act.
mi:HB 4011.summary: As introduced, authorizes the State Administrative Board to convey about 118 acres of state land in Arenac County, site of the closed Standish Maximum Correctional Facility, by competitive sale, sale to local government, or transfer.

mi:HB 4135.title: Property: conveyance of state property; conveyance of certain state-owned property in Jackson County; provide for. Creates land transfer act.
mi:HB 4135.summary: As introduced, authorizes the State Administrative Board to convey about 81 acres of state land in Jackson County, with Jackson County given first right to buy it for $1.00 within two years of enactment.

mi:HB 4598.title: Crimes: organized; violations of the organized retail crime act; expand. Amends sec. 4 of 2012 PA 455 (MCL 752.1084).
mi:HB 4598.summary: As introduced, makes it organized retail crime, a felony punishable by up to 5 years, to knowingly and with intent to defraud acquire, alter, or exploit gift cards or gift card redemption information.

mi:HB 4599.title: Crimes: organized; gift card fraud; provide for. Amends 2012 PA 455 (MCL 752.1081 - 752.1087) by adding sec. 3a.   TIE BAR WITH: HB 4598'25
mi:HB 4599.summary: As introduced, defines gift card, gift card redemption information, and closed- and open-loop gift cards for use in HB 4598's gift card fraud offenses; takes effect only if both bills are enacted.

mi:HB 4678.title: Agriculture: weights and measures; certain definitions; provide for. Amends 1964 PA 283 (MCL 290.601 - 290.635) by adding sec. 28g.   TIE BAR WITH: HB 4679'25
mi:HB 4678.summary: As introduced, lets qualified equipment rental businesses sell motor fuel to refill rented equipment at a flat rate or per-gallon fee, if stated in the rental contract.

mi:HB 4679.title: Agriculture: weights and measures; certain definitions; provide for. Amends secs. 10 & 28c of 1964 PA 283 (MCL 290.610 & 290.628c).   TIE BAR WITH: HB 4678'25
mi:HB 4679.summary: As introduced, says the Department of Agriculture and Rural Development need not inspect and test each qualified fuel dispenser, and treats testing requirements as met if the dispenser complies with HB 4678 and federal transportation rules.

mi:HB 4703.title: Insurance: health insurers; coverage for group prenatal care services; require. Amends 1956 PA 218 (MCL 500.100 - 500.8302) by adding sec. 3406ss.
mi:HB 4703.summary: As introduced, requires health insurance policies issued or renewed in Michigan on or after January 1, 2026 to cover group prenatal care services.

mi:HB 5120.title: Civil procedure: service of process; cost for service of process for personal protection orders; eliminate. Amends secs. 2559 & 2950 of 1961 PA 236 (MCL 600.2559 & 600.2950).   TIE BAR WITH: HB 5121'25,  HB 6033'26
mi:HB 5120.summary: Under proposed substitute H-1, bars courts and police from charging personal protection order petitioners service fees, and sets requirements for the contents and service of domestic relationship protection orders.

mi:HB 5121.title: Civil procedure: service of process; cost for service of process for personal protection orders; eliminate. Amends sec. 2950a of 1961 PA 236 (MCL 600.2950a) & adds secs. 2950d & 2950p.   TIE BAR WITH: HB 5120'25,  HB 6033'26
mi:HB 5121.summary: Under proposed substitute H-1, bars courts and police from charging personal protection order petitioners service fees, creates a fund from which police may collect a $50 service fee, and sets rules for serving orders.

mi:HB 5356.title: Vehicles: title; requirements for transfer of title by a dealer; provide for. Amends 14, 41a, 78, 217, 217c, 233, 233a, 233b, 234, 238, 239, 240, 248, 248a, 248j, 249, 250, 258, 801b, 806 & 810a of 1949 PA 300 (MCL 257.14 et seq.) & adds sec. 9b.
mi:HB 5356.summary: As introduced, makes several Vehicle Code changes, including raising the maximum police salvage inspection fee from $100 to $125 and raising title bond value thresholds to $5,000 for licensed new vehicle dealers.

mi:HB 5482.title: State agencies (existing): generally; plans to correct audit recommendations; require notification to the legislature if the executive branch fails to prepare. Amends sec. 242 of 1984 PA 431 (MCL 18.1242).
mi:HB 5482.summary: Removes the requirement that appropriation acts for capital outlay projects include State Building Authority rental payments for the authorized projects.

mi:HB 5485.summary: As introduced, revises Michigan's dam safety rules, including new definitions, changing the impounding-capacity threshold for covered dams to 15 acre-feet, and amending hazard-potential classifications and emergency action plan requirements.

mi:HB 5514.title: Children: other; prohibition of use of certain restraints while transporting youths to certain qualified residential treatment programs; provide for. Creates new act.
mi:HB 5514.summary: As introduced, bars youth transportation companies from using blindfolds, hoods, handcuffs, chains or other mechanical or physical restraints on youths being taken to qualified residential treatment programs, with exceptions.

mi:HB 6033.title: Civil procedure: costs and fees; fees for service of process; revise. Amends sec. 2559 of 1961 PA 236 (MCL 600.2559).
mi:HB 6033.summary: As introduced, bars courts and police from charging personal protection order petitioners service fees and raises existing service-of-process fees in other cases.

mi:HB 6127.title: Gaming: other; expenditures in the internet gaming fund; modify. Amends secs. 14 & 16 of 2019 PA 152 (MCL 432.314 & 432.316).
mi:HB 6127.summary: Raises the annual Internet Gaming Fund allocation to the first responder presumed coverage fund from $2.0 million to up to $7.0 million (half its claim and administrative costs), and allocates $1.0 million a year for tribal governments.

mi:HB 6259.title: Criminal procedure: sentencing guidelines; sentencing guidelines for criminal sexual conduct; modify. Amends sec. 16y, ch. XVII of 1927 PA 175 (MCL 777.16y).   TIE BAR WITH: HB 6261'26,  HB 6262'26
mi:HB 6259.summary: As introduced, reclassifies second- and third-degree criminal sexual conduct in the sentencing guidelines as Class A felonies with a statutory maximum of life; takes effect only if HB 6261 and 6262 are enacted.

mi:HB 6260.title: Crimes: criminal sexual conduct; penalties for criminal sexual conduct in the first degree; modify. Amends sec. 520b of 1931 PA 328 (MCL 750.520b).
mi:HB 6260.summary: As introduced, sets a 15-year mandatory minimum sentence for first-degree criminal sexual conduct, which already carries a maximum of life.

mi:HB 6261.title: Crimes: criminal sexual conduct; penalties for criminal sexual conduct in the second degree; modify. Amends sec. 520c of 1931 PA 328 (MCL 750.520c).
mi:HB 6261.summary: As introduced, sets a 10-year mandatory minimum and raises the maximum from 15 years to life for second-degree criminal sexual conduct.

mi:HB 6262.title: Crimes: criminal sexual conduct; penalties for criminal sexual conduct in the third degree; modify. Amends sec. 520d of 1931 PA 328 (MCL 750.520d).
mi:HB 6262.summary: As introduced, sets a 5-year mandatory minimum and raises the maximum from 15 years to life for third-degree criminal sexual conduct.

mi:HB 6263.title: Crimes: criminal sexual conduct; penalties for criminal sexual conduct in the fourth degree; modify. Amends sec. 520e of 1931 PA 328 (MCL 750.520e).
mi:HB 6263.summary: As introduced, changes fourth-degree criminal sexual conduct from a misdemeanor to a felony, keeping the 2-year maximum prison term.

mi:HB 6282.title: Public employees and officers: ethics; moratorium on former legislators accepting employment with an entity that receives a grant from the utility consumer participation board; provide for. Creates new act.
mi:HB 6282.summary: As introduced, bars former state legislators for two years after leaving office from working for an entity receiving a Utility Consumer Participation Board grant; violations are misdemeanors with up to 90 days in jail or a $1,000 fine.

mi:HB 6302.title: Education: school districts; requirement to display an American flag in classrooms; provide for. Amends sec. 1347 of 1976 PA 451 (MCL 380.1347).
mi:HB 6302.summary: As introduced, requires school boards to ensure a U.S. flag is displayed, hoisted, draped, or placed on a stand in a prominent location in each classroom where students recite the Pledge of Allegiance.

mi:HB 6309.title: Highways: memorial; portion of M-86; designate as the "Casey Rice Memorial Highway". Amends 2001 PA 142 (MCL 250.1001 - 250.2092) by adding sec. 116.
mi:HB 6309.summary: As introduced, designates M-86 in Branch County between US-12 and Arbogast Road as the "Casey Rice Memorial Highway."

mi:HR 373.title: A resolution to condemn socialism, the platform of the Democratic Socialists for America, and politicians who espouse socialist views, and to oppose the implementation of socialist policies in the state of Michigan and the United States.
mi:HR 373.summary: Condemns socialism, the platform of the Democratic Socialists for America, and politicians who espouse socialist views, and opposes socialist policies in Michigan and the United States.

mi:SB 198.title: Occupations: vehicles, dealers, and repair facilities; requirements for automobile dealer data collection; provide for. Creates new act.
mi:SB 198.summary: As introduced, bars vehicle manufacturers and third parties from accessing, sharing or using protected dealer data, including consumer and diagnostic data, without the dealer's written consent, and from limiting dealers' use of it.

mi:SB 217.title: Traffic control: accidents; penalties for moving violation causing physical injury or death to a vulnerable roadway user; enhance. Amends sec. 12e, ch. XVII of 1927 PA 175 (MCL 777.12e).   TIE BAR WITH: SB 0216'25
mi:SB 217.summary: As introduced, adds the new felonies for moving violations that seriously injure or kill vulnerable roadway users, such as pedestrians, to the sentencing guidelines; tied to SB 216.

mi:SB 373.title: Housing: landlord and tenants; limitations on fees charged to tenants; provide for. Amends sec. 3 of 1978 PA 454 (MCL 554.633).
mi:SB 373.summary: As introduced, bars a rental agreement from charging an extra fee on every allowed rent payment method, so an agreement allowing multiple methods must offer at least one without an added charge.

mi:SB 413.title: Health occupations: psychologists; requirements for practice by limited licensed psychologist; modify. Amends secs. 18221, 18223, 18233 & 18237 of 1978 PA 368 (MCL 333.18221 et seq.).
mi:SB 413.summary: As introduced, raises the supervised postgraduate experience required for a limited-license psychologist from one year to two years and 3,000-4,000 hours, lets limited licensees practice without supervision, and changes the Board of Psychology's membership.

mi:SB 433.title: State agencies (existing): health and human services; educational materials regarding health dangers for youth using high-potency THC and cannabis products; require the department to provide. Amends 1976 PA 451 (MCL 380.1 - 380.1852) by adding sec. 1509.
mi:SB 433.summary: As introduced, requires the Department of Health and Human Services to develop a notice on the dangers of high-potency THC cannabis and vaping and on prevention and treatment resources, which schools must give parents by October 1 each year from 2026-27.

mi:SB 478.title: Property: conveyance of state property; transfer of certain state-owned property in Livingston County; provide for. Creates land transfer act.
mi:SB 478.summary: As introduced, authorizes the State Administrative Board to transfer about 93 acres in Green Oak Township, Livingston County, from the Department of Corrections to the Department of Military and Veterans Affairs, which may use it for a National Guard readiness center.

mi:SB 729.title: State finance: authorities; outstanding obligations of the state building authority; provide exception to the limit of. Amends sec. 8 of 1964 PA 183 (MCL 830.418).
mi:SB 729.summary: As introduced, exempts $421.3 million of State Building Authority bonds issued in June 2025 from counting toward the Authority's $2.7 billion cap on outstanding debt.

mi:SB 791.title: Highways: memorial; portion of I-475; designate as the "St. John Street Community Memorial Highway". Amends 2001 PA 142 (MCL 250.1001 - 250.2092) by adding sec. 124.
mi:SB 791.summary: As introduced, designates the portion of I-475 in Genesee County from Hamilton Avenue north to a quarter mile past Stewart Avenue as the "St. John Street Community Memorial Highway."

mi:SB 947.title: Natural resources: inland lakes; dam safety regulations; provide for. Amends and adds (See bill).   TIE BAR WITH: HB 5485'26
mi:SB 947.summary: As introduced, brings dams licensed under the Federal Power Act under state environmental department jurisdiction, raises dam permit fees, increases inspection frequency, and requires a dam registration process.

mn:HF 1849.title: Term limits provided for governor and lieutenant governor, and constitutional amendment proposed.
mn:HF 1849.summary: Proposes a state constitutional amendment, for the 2026 ballot, limiting a person to being elected governor no more than twice and lieutenant governor no more than twice, counting terms from the 2026 election.

mn:HF 5084.title: Preborn child given recognized right to life, and constitutional amendment proposed.
mn:HF 5084.summary: As introduced, proposes a state constitutional amendment for the 2026 ballot stating that a preborn child has the right to life, while allowing medical treatment to save the life or preserve the health of the pregnant person.

mn:HF 5140.title: Ownership, possession, and sale of semiautomatic military-style assault weapons and large-capacity magazines regulated; provisions for possessing dangerous weapons in schools, negligently storing firearms, and reporting on law enforcement firearms discharge modified; ghost guns criminalized; other gun safety provisions modified; and money appropriated.
mn:HF 5140.summary: As introduced, regulates semiautomatic military-style assault weapons and large-capacity magazines, criminalizes ghost guns, re-enacts the binary trigger ban, changes firearm storage, school weapons and extreme risk protection order rules, and appropriates money.

mn:SF 2077.title: Omnibus Outdoor Heritage Fund, Legacy and Lands bill
mn:SF 2077.summary: Appropriates $191.1 million from the Outdoor Heritage Fund for fiscal year 2027, changes state land and DNR licensing provisions, appropriates $80,000 to the Agricultural Utilization Research Institute, and extends unemployment benefits for certain iron ore mining workers.

mn:SF 2373.title: Omnibus Labor policy bill
mn:SF 2373.summary: Exempts minor league baseball players from minimum wage and overtime rules, changes construction code and licensing provisions, extends unemployment insurance for certain iron ore workers, and funds the Agricultural Utilization Research Institute.

mn:SF 3720.title: 2026 recommendations adoption of the Workers' Compensation Advisory Council
mn:SF 3720.summary: Changes workers' compensation law, including what an insurer owes when leaving the reinsurance association, how an insolvent member's liabilities are handled, legal fee limits and permanent partial disability compensation.

mn:SF 4282.title: Various agency forecast adjustments
mn:SF 4282.summary: Adjusts fiscal year 2026 and 2027 education, human services and Metro Mobility appropriations to match the February 2026 forecast, and changes K-12 programs, including new aid for Tribal contract schools and extended restroom grants.

mn:SF 4401.title: Omnibus Cannabis bill
mn:SF 4401.summary: Makes changes to Minnesota's cannabis law, including creating a cannabis macrobusiness license, streamlining adult-use and medical cannabis rules, requiring endorsements for authorized activities, changing labeling rules, and letting hemp license holders also hold cannabis licenses.

mn:SF 4476.title: Omnibus Human Services supplemental appropriations
mn:SF 4476.summary: Makes human services supplemental budget changes, including Medicaid continuity of care, long-term care facility rules, background studies, behavioral health, electronic visit verification, and appropriations for the Department of Human Services and other agencies.

mn:SF 4612.title: Omnibus Health and Human Services supplemental appropriations
mn:SF 4612.summary: Makes health and children and families supplemental budget changes, including Department of Health, hospital stabilization, health licensing board, medical assistance fraud prevention and child care licensing provisions, plus forecast adjustments and agency appropriations.

nc:HB 1035.title: Various Local Election Changes III.
nc:HB 1035.summary: Moves municipal elections to even-numbered years for all municipalities in Catawba and McDowell Counties and several towns starting in 2028, and New Bern in 2030. Also extends some town officers' terms from two to four years and changes New Bern's election method.

nc:HB 1089.title: Constitutional Amendment Property Tax Levy Limit.
nc:HB 1089.summary: Puts a question on the ballot on amending the state constitution to require the General Assembly to pass laws limiting how much counties and cities can raise their property tax levies.

nc:HB 133.title: NC Farmland and Military Protection Act.
nc:HB 133.summary: Bars foreign parties tied to adversarial governments from holding interests in agricultural land or land within 50 miles of a military installation. Existing holders must register, and later acquisitions must be sold within one year.

nc:HB 162.title: Parking Lot Reform/Stormwater Control.
nc:HB 162.summary: Bars most local governments outside the coastal area from requiring a minimum number of off-street parking spaces, and lets local governments offer optional incentives for extra stormwater controls. Also changes stormwater rules for existing impervious surface.

nc:HB 198.title: ABC Omnibus of 2026.
nc:HB 198.summary: Changes alcohol law so the ABC Commission, not enforcement officers, must notify a permit holder within five business days of receiving a law enforcement report of violations on the premises.

nc:HB 308.title: 2026 Criminal Law Changes.
nc:HB 308.summary: Raises penalties for assault with serious bodily injury and for strangulation, creates a felony of habitual domestic violence, clarifies domestic violence misdemeanor and expunction provisions, and removes the default of concurrent sentences.

nc:HB 315.title: Prohibit Litigation Investments/Amend Workers' Compensation Benefits.
nc:HB 315.summary: Makes it unlawful to provide or engage in litigation investment in civil cases, and raises workers' compensation amounts, including the minimum weekly total-disability rate from $30 to $50 and disfigurement caps phased up to $56,000 and $28,000.

nc:HB 517.title: Modify Nonprofit Corporations Act/Charitable Organizations.
nc:HB 517.summary: Changes the nonprofit corporation law: allows new kinds of mergers and asset sales, requires annual reports to the Secretary of State, allows domestication, requires at least 3 natural persons on a nonprofit board, and aligns charity disclosures with federal rules.

nc:HB 727.title: Limit Medicaid Reimb. for Facility Fees.
nc:HB 727.summary: Directs the Department of Health and Human Services to stop Medicaid from reimbursing facility fees unless the service is provided at a hospital's main building or nearby structures, a facility with an emergency department, or an ambulatory surgical facility.

nc:HB 87.title: Educational Choice for Children Act (ECCA).
nc:HB 87.summary: Has North Carolina opt into the federal tax credit for donations to scholarship granting organizations, and directs the State Education Assistance Authority to carry out the state's participation in the program.

nc:HB 936.title: Robocall Solicitation Modifications.
nc:HB 936.summary: Applies state telephone solicitation rules to robocalls and text messages, requires prior express written consent for solicitations, bans impersonating government officials in them, and counts civil penalties per violation within a single solicitation.

nc:SB 1057.title: Required Disclosures/Proxy Advisory Services.
nc:SB 1057.summary: Requires proxy advisors to make certain disclosures to shareholders and company boards when they recommend against company management or policy, under a new Proxy Advisor Transparency Act.

nc:SB 1082.title: NC Right to Work Amendment.
nc:SB 1082.summary: Puts a constitutional amendment on the 2026 general election ballot declaring that the right to work may not be denied or abridged because of membership or nonmembership in a labor union or organization.

nc:SB 484.title: Clarify Tourism-Related Expenditures.
nc:SB 484.summary: Bars local occupancy tax proceeds labeled tourism-related expenditures from paying for services normally funded by a local government's general fund, such as trash collection, police, emergency services, affordable housing or education, unless a local act allows it.

nc:SB 528.title: Health and Human Services Revisions.
nc:SB 528.summary: Makes several health and human services changes, including wider access to birth certificate data for research and public health, a veterans brain-stimulation pilot program, crisis-line information at schools and colleges, and insurance coverage of prosthetics.

nc:SB 808.title: Board of Cosmetic Art Examiners Amendments.
nc:SB 808.summary: Changes cosmetic art licensing: cuts the natural hair care specialist curriculum from 300 to 150 hours, creates a hair braider certification and hair design licenses, lowers teacher license hours to 500, and allows mobile cosmetic art shops.

nc:SB 858.title: GSC Add Member from High Point Law School.
nc:SB 858.summary: Adds a 14th member to the General Statutes Commission, appointed by the dean of the High Point University School of Law, with a first term from September 1, 2026 to August 31, 2029.

nc:SB 992.title: Truth in Taxation.
nc:SB 992.summary: Requires local governments to follow added procedures to adopt a property tax rate above the revenue-neutral rate in a reappraisal year, and raises the fee to reinstate an expired real estate appraiser trainee registration, license or certificate.

nd:HB 1003.title: AN ACT to provide an appropriation for defraying the expenses of the attorney general; to amend and reenact sections 31-01-16, 54-12-11, 54-12-30, and 54-27-25 of the North Dakota Century Code, relating to compensation and mileage and travel expenses for witnesses, the salary of the attorney general, twenty-four seven sobriety program fees, and the tobacco settlement trust fund; to provide for a report; to provide for a transfer; and to provide an exemption.
nd:HB 1003.summary: Appropriates about $114.7 million to the Attorney General for 2025-27, including human trafficking victim and forensic nurse examiner grant programs, and sets the Attorney General's salary and witness pay and mileage rules.

nd:HB 1004.title: AN ACT to provide an appropriation for defraying the expenses of the state auditor; and to amend and reenact section 54-10-10 of the North Dakota Century Code, relating to the salary of the state auditor.
nd:HB 1004.summary: Appropriates about $18.2 million to the State Auditor for 2025-27 and sets the State Auditor's salary.

nd:HB 1005.title: AN ACT to provide an appropriation for defraying the expenses of the state treasurer; to amend and reenact section 54-11-13 of the North Dakota Century Code, relating to the salary of the state treasurer; and to declare an emergency.
nd:HB 1005.summary: Appropriates about $3.5 million to the State Treasurer for 2025-27 and sets the State Treasurer's salary.

nd:HB 1006.title: AN ACT to provide an appropriation for defraying the expenses of the office of the tax commissioner and for payment of state reimbursement under the homestead tax credit, disabled veterans' tax credit, and primary residence credit; to amend and reenact section 57-01-04 of the North Dakota Century Code, relating to the salary of the state tax commissioner; to provide an exemption; and to provide for a transfer.
nd:HB 1006.summary: Appropriates about $127.7 million from all funds to the Tax Commissioner for 2025-27, including reimbursement of the homestead and disabled veterans' tax credits, and sets the Tax Commissioner's salary.

nd:HB 1008.title: AN ACT to provide an appropriation for defraying the expenses of the public service commission; to amend and reenact sections 49-01-05 and 57-43.2-19 of the North Dakota Century Code, relating to the salaries of the public service commissioners and deposits of special fuels excise taxes; and to provide loan authorization.
nd:HB 1008.summary: Appropriates about $23.5 million to the Public Service Commission for 2025-27, sets commissioners' salaries, and authorizes a loan for a rail rate complaint case.

nd:HB 1009.title: AN ACT to provide an appropriation for defraying the expenses of the agriculture commissioner; to amend and reenact section 4.1-01-02 of the North Dakota Century Code, relating to the salary of the agriculture commissioner; to provide for a transfer; to provide for a report; to provide an exemption; and to declare an emergency.
nd:HB 1009.summary: Appropriates about $55.2 million to the Agriculture Commissioner for 2025-27, including several fund transfers, and sets the commissioner's salary.

nd:HB 1010.title: AN ACT to provide an appropriation for defraying the expenses of the insurance commissioner; to create and enact a new section to chapter 26.1-23.1 of the North Dakota Century Code, relating to a government self-insurance pool report; to amend and reenact subsection 8 of section 10-04-10 and section 26.1-01-09 of the North Dakota Century Code, relating to fees charged by the securities division and the salary of the insurance commissioner; and to provide for a legislative management report.
nd:HB 1010.summary: Appropriates about $20.8 million to the Insurance Commissioner for 2025-27, requires government self-insurance pools to report to the Legislative Management every even-numbered year, and changes securities division fees and the commissioner's salary.

nd:HB 1013.title: AN ACT to provide an appropriation for defraying the expenses of the department of public instruction, the center for distance education, the state library, the school for the deaf, and North Dakota vision services - school for the blind; to create and enact a new section to chapter 15.1-07 of the North Dakota Century Code, relating to the collection of free or reduced-price meal eligibility information; to amend and reenact sections 15.1-02-02 and 15.1-27-16 of the North Dakota Century Code, relating to the salary of the superintendent of public instruction and administrative cost-sharing; to provide for a transfer; to provide a report; to provide an exemption; and to provide an effective date.
nd:HB 1013.summary: Appropriates about $3.01 billion to the Department of Public Instruction for 2025-27, plus funds for the school for the deaf, state library and others, including $6 million for school meal grants, and requires districts to collect meal eligibility data electronically.

nd:HB 1015.title: AN ACT to provide an appropriation for defraying the expenses of the various divisions under the supervision of the director of the office of management and budget; to create and enact a new section to chapter 54-44 of the North Dakota Century Code, relating to a state facility maintenance fund; to amend and reenact subsection 1 of section 10-30.5-02 of the North Dakota Century Code and section 9 of House Bill No. 1012, as approved by the sixty-ninth Legislative Assembly, relating to the North Dakota development fund and infant and toddler care provider support payments; to repeal section 11-38-08 of the North Dakota Century Code, relating to county achievement days; to provide for a transfer; to authorize a line of credit; to provide an exemption; to provide for a report; and to declare an emergency.
nd:HB 1015.summary: Appropriates about $410 million to the Office of Management and Budget for 2025-27, creates a state facility maintenance fund, sets guidelines for state employee raises averaging 3% a year, and allows a $100 million Bank of North Dakota credit line for the state hospital project.

nd:HB 1016.title: AN ACT to provide an appropriation for defraying the expenses of the office of the adjutant general; to provide a statement of legislative intent; to provide an exemption; and to declare an emergency.
nd:HB 1016.summary: Appropriates funding to the Adjutant General's office for 2025-27, including disaster costs and a veterans' cemetery, and states intent to buy up to 1,600 acres and lease the rest, up to 6,000 total, for Camp Grafton without eminent domain.

nd:HB 1018.title: AN ACT to provide an appropriation for defraying the expenses of the state historical society; to amend and reenact section 55-01-02.1 of the North Dakota Century Code, relating to jurisdiction of the heritage center; to authorize a Bank of North Dakota line of credit; and to declare an emergency.
nd:HB 1018.summary: Appropriates about $114.2 million to the State Historical Society for 2025-27, authorizes a Bank of North Dakota line of credit for a military gallery, and changes provisions on the heritage center's jurisdiction.

nd:HB 1019.title: AN ACT to provide an appropriation for defraying the expenses of the parks and recreation department; to create and enact a new section to chapter 55-08 of the North Dakota Century Code, relating to the creation and naming of state parks; to provide for a transfer; to provide for a report; and to provide an exemption.
nd:HB 1019.summary: Appropriates about $59 million to the Parks and Recreation Department for 2025-27, plus $3.1 million for the International Peace Garden, and requires legislative approval before a state agency creates or renames a state park.

nd:HB 1022.title: AN ACT to provide an appropriation for defraying the expenses of the retirement and investment office.
nd:HB 1022.summary: Appropriates about $16.5 million from special funds to the Retirement and Investment Office for 2025-27, with 35 full-time positions.

nd:HB 1027.title: AN ACT to amend and reenact sections 26.1-01-03, 26.1-22-01, 26.1-22-02, 26.1-22-02.1, 26.1-22-03.1, 26.1-22-09, 26.1-22-10, 26.1-22-11, 26.1-22-14, 26.1-22-16, 26.1-22-17, 26.1-22-21, and 26.1-22-22, subdivisions a and c of subsection 1 of section 26.1-23.1-01, and section 37-03-13 of the North Dakota Century Code, relating to changing the administration of the state fire and tornado fund from the insurance commissioner to the office of management and budget; to repeal sections 26.1-22-03, 26.1-22-05, 26.1-22-06, 26.1-22-06.1, 26.1-22-08, 26.1-22-10.1, 26.1-22-13, 26.1-22-15, 26.1-22-18, 26.1-22-19, and 26.1-22-21.1 of the North Dakota Century Code, relating to the administration of the state fire and tornado fund; to provide for a legislative management study; and to provide a continuing appropriation.
nd:HB 1027.summary: Moves administration of the state fire and tornado fund from the Insurance Commissioner to the Office of Management and Budget and repeals several related sections.

nd:HB 1119.title: AN ACT to provide for a legislative management study regarding child care provider licensing; to provide for a program evaluation regarding child care services; and to create a child care services licensing advisory committee.
nd:HB 1119.summary: Directs the Legislative Management to study child care provider licensing laws and rules, allows a program evaluation of child care services, and creates a child care services licensing advisory committee.
