nd:HB 1126.title: AN ACT to create and enact eleven new sections to chapter 43-11 of the North Dakota Century Code, relating to salon and school inspections, nursing home, basic care facility, and assisted living facility salons, military and military spouse reciprocity licensure, advanced esthetician licensing and late renewals for establishments and schools; to amend and reenact sections 43-11-01, 43-11-02, 43-11-03, 43-11-04, 43-11-05, 43-11-06, 43-11-08, 43-11-10, 43-11-11, 43-11-13, 43-11-14, 43-11-15, 43-11-16, 43-11-16.1, 43-11-19, 43-11-20.3, 43-11-21, 43-11-23, 43-11-24, 43-11-25, 43-11-26, 43-11-27, 43-11-28, and 43-11-29 of the North Dakota Century Code, relating to the practice and licensure of cosmetologists, estheticians, advanced estheticians, manicurists, and instructors; to repeal sections 43-11-11.1, 43-11-17, and 43-11-27.1 of the North Dakota Century Code, relating to the use of brush rollers, licenses issued for schools and salons, and esthetician and manicurist licensing qualifications and fees; to provide a penalty; and to provide an effective date.
nd:HB 1126.summary: Changes cosmetology law to add salon and school inspections, services for residents of nursing homes and assisted living, license reciprocity for military members and spouses, an advanced esthetician license, and late renewals.

nd:HB 1130.title: A BILL for an Act to amend and reenact section 15.1-27-04.1 of the North Dakota Century Code, relating to the option for a school district to reduce its local contribution deduction in the school state aid formula by the percentage of the local contribution which comes from in lieu of revenue.
nd:HB 1130.summary: Changes the school state aid formula's local contribution deduction, including how mills levied for sinking and interest fund (bond repayment) purposes reduce the local revenue counted against state aid.

nd:HB 1139.title: AN ACT to create and enact a new subsection to section 57-39.2-04 of the North Dakota Century Code, relating to a sales tax exemption for fire departments; and to provide an effective date.
nd:HB 1139.summary: Exempts sales to approved fire departments and fire districts, for fire protection services, from state sales tax, for sales after June 30, 2025.

nd:HB 1160.title: AN ACT to create and enact a new section to chapter 15.1-07 of the North Dakota Century Code, relating to the use of personal electronic devices during instructional time.
nd:HB 1160.summary: Requires school districts to adopt policies keeping students' phones and other personal electronic devices turned off and locked away or inaccessible during instructional time, with enforcement provisions and exceptions for medical devices and school-approved devices.

nd:HB 1168.title: A BILL for an Act to create and enact two new sections to chapter 54-27, a new section to chapter 57-02, and a new section to chapter 57-15 of the North Dakota Century Code, relating to a legacy earnings fund, a legacy property tax relief fund, a primary residence certification, and a limitation on property tax levies without voter approval; to amend and reenact section 6-09.4-10.1, subsection 1 of section 21-10-06, sections 40-40-06, 54-27-19.3, and 57-02-01, subdivision c of subsection 1 of section 57-02-08.1, subdivision b of subsection 2 of section 57-02-08.1, section 57-02-08.8, section 57-02-08.9 as amended by section 1 of Senate Bill No. 2201, as approved by the sixty-ninth legislative assembly, sections 57-02-08.10, 57-02-27, 57-02-27.1, 57-02-53, 57-09-04, 57-11-03, 57-12-06, 57-15-02.2, 57-15-14.2, and 57-20-07.1 of the North Dakota Century Code, relating to funds invested by the state investment board, property tax definitions, the homestead tax credit and renters refund, the property tax credit for disabled veterans, the primary residence credit, property classifications, assessment and budget hearing notices to property owners, school district levies, and the property tax statement; to repeal sections 21-10-12 and 21-10-13 of the North Dakota Century Code, relating to legacy fund definitions and the legacy earnings fund; to provide a statement of legislative intent; to provide for a legislative management study, to provide an appropriation; to provide an effective date; to provide an expiration date; and to declare an emergency.
nd:HB 1168.summary: Creates a legacy earnings fund fed by a 7% draw on the Legacy Fund and a legacy property tax relief fund. Requires primary residence certification and limits property tax levies without voter approval.

nd:HB 1176.title: AN ACT to create and enact two new sections to chapter 54-27, a new section to chapter 57-02, and a new section to chapter 57-15 of the North Dakota Century Code, relating to a legacy earnings fund, a legacy property tax relief fund, a primary residence certification, and a limitation on property tax levies without voter approval; to amend and reenact section 6-09.4-10.1, subsection 1 of section 21-10-06, sections 40-40-06, 54-27-19.3, and 57-02-01, subdivision b of subsection 2 of section 57-02-08.1, section 57-02-08.8, section 57-02-08.9 as amended by section 1 of Senate Bill No. 2201, as approved by the sixty-ninth legislative assembly, sections 57-02-08.10, 57-02-27, 57-02-27.1, 57-02-53, 57-09-04, 57-11-03, 57-12-06, 57-15-02.2, 57-15-14.2, and 57-20-07.1 of the North Dakota Century Code, relating to funds invested by the state investment board, property tax definitions, the renters refund, the property tax credit for disabled veterans, the primary residence credit, property classifications, assessment and budget hearing notices to property owners, school district levies, and the property tax statement; to repeal sections 21-10-12 and 21-10-13 of the North Dakota Century Code, relating to legacy fund definitions and the legacy earnings fund; to provide for a legislative management study; to provide for a legislative management report; to provide an appropriation; to provide an exemption; to provide an effective date; to provide an expiration date; and to declare an emergency.
nd:HB 1176.summary: Creates a legacy earnings fund fed by an 8% draw on the Legacy Fund and a legacy property tax relief fund. Requires primary residence certification and limits property tax levies without voter approval.

nd:HB 1181.title: AN ACT to amend and reenact section 1-01-34 of the North Dakota Century Code, relating to gender usage in the North Dakota Century Code.
nd:HB 1181.summary: Provides that words of one gender in state law include the other genders, and that words referring to an individual's gender mean the individual's sex.

nd:HB 1193.title: AN ACT to provide an appropriation to the attorney general for a peace officer and correctional officer appreciation grant program; and to provide for a legislative management report.
nd:HB 1193.summary: Appropriates $3.5 million to the Attorney General for grants to city and county law enforcement agencies, divided by their number of licensed peace officers and correctional officers.

nd:HB 1203.title: AN ACT to create and enact section 19-24.1-24.1 and a new subsection to section 19-24.1-36 of the North Dakota Century Code, relating to regulating edible medical marijuana products; and to amend and reenact section 19-24.1-01 of the North Dakota Century Code, relating to definitions of medical marijuana products.
nd:HB 1203.summary: Requires state approval before a manufacturer or dispensary may make or sell edible medical marijuana products, and sets limits of 50 milligrams of THC per package, child-resistant resealable packaging, plain text labels and no marketing to minors.

nd:HB 1209.title: AN ACT to provide for a legislative management report relating to a foreign adversary threat assessment conducted by the department of emergency services.
nd:HB 1209.summary: Requires the Department of Emergency Services to assess which sectors are most vulnerable to foreign adversary influence, including beyond land purchases, and propose mitigation strategies, and to report to the Legislative Management.

nd:HB 1216.title: AN ACT to create and enact a new section to chapter 26.1-36 of the North Dakota Century Code, relating to out-of-pocket expenses for prescription drugs; to amend and reenact section 26.1-36.6-03 of the North Dakota Century Code, relating to self-insurance health care plans; to provide for application; and to provide an effective date.
nd:HB 1216.summary: Requires health plans that cover prescription drugs to count amounts paid by or for the enrollee, including through cost-sharing assistance programs, toward the enrollee's out-of-pocket maximum and cost-sharing for those drugs.

nd:HB 1218.title: AN ACT to create and enact a new section to chapter 61-02 of the North Dakota Century Code, relating to a temporary moratorium on conducting an economic analysis for assessment drain projects; to amend and reenact section 61-02-01.3 of the North Dakota Century Code, relating to comprehensive water development plans; to provide for a legislative management study; and to provide an expiration date.
nd:HB 1218.summary: Bars the State Water Commission and Department of Water Resources from conducting economic analyses for assessment drain projects between August 1, 2025 and July 31, 2027, and orders a study of the analysis formula.

nd:HB 1226.title: AN ACT to amend and reenact section 12.1-31-15 of the North Dakota Century Code, relating to wearing a mask in a public place.
nd:HB 1226.summary: Adds a ban on wearing a face covering to hide one's identity while gathering in a public place with others similarly covered, except at Halloween, masquerade or similar celebrations. A violation is a class A misdemeanor.

nd:HB 1234.title: AN ACT to provide a transfer from the strategic investment and improvements fund to the public employees retirement system fund; and to provide for a statement of legislative intent.
nd:HB 1234.summary: Transfers $25 million from the strategic investment and improvements fund to the public employees retirement system fund to reduce the unfunded liability of its main defined benefit plan.

nd:HB 1279.title: AN ACT to amend and reenact sections 57-60-02, 57-60-02.1, 57-60-02.2, 57-60-14, and 57-61-01 of the North Dakota Century Code, relating to a partial exemption from the coal conversion facilities tax and the imposition of a lignite research tax, allocation of the coal conversion facilities privilege tax and the lignite research tax, and an exemption from the coal severance tax; to repeal section 57-60-02.2 of the North Dakota Century Code, relating to the exemption from the coal conversion facilities tax and the imposition of a lignite research tax; to provide an effective date; to provide a contingent effective date; and to provide an expiration date.
nd:HB 1279.summary: Changes the coal conversion facility tax exemption to a partial exemption stepping down from 90% to 35% of the state share by 2030-31, adds a 5% lignite research tax, and sends the remaining state share to the Legacy Fund.

nd:HB 1300.title: A BILL for an Act to create and enact a new section to chapter 54-03 of the North Dakota Century Code, relating to legislative term limits.
nd:HB 1300.summary: Provides that the years of service counted toward the constitutional legislative term limit begin when a person is first elected or appointed to the Legislature after January 1, 2023.

nd:HB 1307.title: AN ACT to amend and reenact sections 11-09.1-04, 11-09.1-05, 40-05.1-05, 40-05.1-06, and 40-49-07 of the North Dakota Century Code, relating to election laws in home rule counties and cities and nominating petition signature thresholds in park districts.
nd:HB 1307.summary: Makes election ordinances in home rule county and city charters void where they conflict with state election law, and lets park boards adopt the same nominating-petition signature threshold as the city.

nd:HB 1322.title: AN ACT to create and enact a new section to chapter 23-27 and a new section to chapter 26.1-47 of the North Dakota Century Code, relating to ambulance service balanced billing and provider reimbursement; to amend and reenact section 23-27-04.8 of the North Dakota Century Code, relating to emergency medical services communication; to provide for a legislative management study; and to provide an appropriation.
nd:HB 1322.summary: Bars non-air ambulance providers from billing patients more than in-network cost-sharing, requires insurers to pay out-of-network ambulance providers the lesser of 250% of the Medicare rate or billed charges, and orders a study of delinquent-billing grants.

nd:HB 1329.title: AN ACT to provide for a legislative management study regarding the establishment of a government spending database.
nd:HB 1329.summary: Directs the Legislative Management to consider studying whether to create a government spending database listing the amount, date, recipient and payer of each expenditure, plus training for school officials on it.

nd:HB 1332.title: AN ACT to amend and reenact section 4.1-01.1-07 of the North Dakota Century Code, relating to a value-added agriculture facility incentive program; to provide for a transfer; to provide an expiration date; and to declare an emergency.
nd:HB 1332.summary: Creates a value-added agriculture production facility incentive grant program, with grants limited to $30 million, funded through the agriculture diversification and development fund. The changes are effective through June 30, 2029.

nd:HB 1361.title: AN ACT to create and enact a new section to chapter 12.1-41 of the North Dakota Century Code, relating to mandatory minimum sentences for human trafficking offenders; and to provide a penalty.
nd:HB 1361.summary: Sets mandatory minimum prison terms without parole for human trafficking offenders: 20 years for a class AA felony, 10 years for a class A felony and 5 years for a class B felony.

nd:HB 1363.title: AN ACT to create and enact a new section to chapter 15.1-02 of the North Dakota Century Code, relating to cardiac emergency response plans for public and nonpublic schools and athletic events.
nd:HB 1363.summary: Requires public and nonpublic schools, starting in 2027-28, to adopt a cardiac emergency response plan using a state template, place and label defibrillators on school grounds, and gives school staff and board members liability immunity when carrying it out.

nd:HB 1382.title: A BILL for an Act to create and enact a new section to chapter 54-27 of the North Dakota Century Code, relating to the creation of the city, county, and township road fund; to amend and reenact subsection 1 of section 39-04-19.2, section 54-27-19, subsection 1 of section 57-43.1-02, and subsection 1 of section 57-43.2-02 of the North Dakota Century Code, relating to the electric and plug-in hybrid vehicle road use fee, the tax imposed on motor vehicle and special fuels, and the highway tax distribution fund; and to provide an effective date.
nd:HB 1382.summary: Raises the annual electric vehicle road use fee to $150 and the plug-in hybrid fee to $60, and creates a city, county and township road fund with changes to how highway tax revenue is distributed.

nd:HB 1417.title: AN ACT to amend and reenact sections 12-59-15 and 12.1-01-04, subdivision b of subsection 3 of section 12.1-22-01, and sections 12.1-32-07, 12.1-32-08, and 29-07-01.1 of the North Dakota Century Code, relating to parole and probation violations and court fees; to provide for a legislative management study; and to provide a penalty.
nd:HB 1417.summary: Changes rules on parole and probation violations, indigent defense cost reimbursement and court fees, and directs the Legislative Management to consider studying court fines and fees.

nd:HB 1425.title: AN ACT to create and enact a new section to chapter 11-16, a new chapter to title 12, and two new sections to chapter 54-23.3 of the North Dakota Century Code, relating to prosecution-led diversion programs, deflection process, and supervision for presentence programs; to provide for a legislative management study; to provide for a legislative management report; and to provide an appropriation.
nd:HB 1425.summary: Lets county state's attorneys run prosecution-led diversion programs, defines a deflection process for people with behavioral health conditions, sets up a corrections supervision pilot in three counties, and provides funding and studies.

nd:HB 1442.title: AN ACT to create and enact a new section to chapter 54-35 of the North Dakota Century Code, relating to the creation of a legislative task force on government efficiency; to provide for a legislative management report; to provide an expiration date; and to declare an emergency.
nd:HB 1442.summary: Creates a legislative task force on government efficiency of state officials and legislators that reviews agency budgets, looks for unnecessary or duplicative programs, may request program audits, and reports annually to the Legislative Management.

nd:HB 1485.title: AN ACT to amend and reenact section 50-24.1-02.6 of the North Dakota Century Code, relating to the personal needs allowance amount for eligible beneficiaries; to provide for an increase in the personal monthly needs allowance; and to provide an appropriation.
nd:HB 1485.summary: Raises the personal monthly needs allowance for Medicaid beneficiaries by $15 for 2025-27 and appropriates $762,894 from the general fund plus $689,466 from federal and special funds.

nd:HB 1487.title: AN ACT to authorize the department of transportation to transfer real property to the office of management and budget; to provide an appropriation; to authorize a line of credit; to provide an exemption; and to declare an emergency.
nd:HB 1487.summary: Orders the Department of Transportation to transfer about 1.25 acres in Ward County to the Office of Management and Budget, which may borrow up to $5.6 million from the Bank of North Dakota to build a Minot facility to lease to state agencies.

nd:HB 1489.title: AN ACT to create and enact chapter 14-07.7 of the North Dakota Century Code, relating to civil protection orders; to amend and reenact sections 11-15-32 and 12-60-23, subsection 2 of section 12.1-17-13, section 14-05-23, subsection 4 of section 14-07.1-01, sections 14-07.1-02.1 and 14-07.1-11, subsection 1 of section 14-07.1-14, section 14-07.1-19, subdivision a of subsection 1 of section 14-07.6-01, subdivision b of subsection 1 of section 15.1-09-33.4, sections 16.1-02-07 and 29-01-15, subdivision g of subsection 1 of section 29-06-15, and subdivision a of subsection 2 of section 47-16-17.1 of the North Dakota Century Code, relating to restraining orders and protection orders; to repeal sections 12.1-31-01.2, 12.1-31.2-01, 14-07.1-02, 14-07.1-03, 14-07.1-03.1, 14-07.1-04, 14-07.1-05, 14-07.1-05.1, 14-07.1-06, 14-07.1-07, and 14-07.1-08 of the North Dakota Century Code, relating to sexual assault restraining orders and domestic violence protection orders; to provide a penalty; and to provide an effective date.
nd:HB 1489.summary: Creates one chapter of law for civil protection orders covering disorderly conduct, domestic violence and sexual assault, setting who may petition and how orders work, and updates related laws to refer to it.

nd:HB 1498.title: AN ACT to amend and reenact sections 15-20.2-07 and 15.1-09-33.1 of the North Dakota Century Code, relating to the powers and duties of center boards and the authority of a school board to pay a first-year signing bonus for teachers; and to declare an emergency.
nd:HB 1498.summary: Lets school boards pay a signing bonus, as a lump sum or in installments up to five years, to licensed staff new to a role in the district, and lets career and technology center boards offer first-year signing bonuses.

nd:HB 1535.title: AN ACT to amend and reenact the new chapter to title 54 as created by section 1 of Senate Bill No. 2098, as approved by the sixty-ninth legislative assembly, and section 54-35-23 of the North Dakota Century Code, relating to a state alert notice system and the committee on tribal and state relations; and to provide for a report.
nd:HB 1535.summary: Revises the state alert notice system created by another bill to include a feather alert for missing or endangered Indigenous individuals, and directs the Tribal and State Relations Committee to evaluate it.

nd:HB 1537.title: AN ACT to amend and reenact section 6-09.4-22 of the North Dakota Century Code, relating to service agreement protection of service during the term of the loan; and to declare an emergency.
nd:HB 1537.summary: Allows a political subdivision and another subdivision to agree on which provides service where a public finance authority loan funded it, but only if the lender is a party and bond payments are safeguarded. Agreements made before 2025 without these terms become voidable.

nd:HB 1540.title: AN ACT to create and enact a new chapter to title 15.1 of the North Dakota Century Code, relating to an education savings account program for students who are not enrolled in public school or a homeschool program; to provide an appropriation; and to provide an effective date.
nd:HB 1540.summary: Creates an education savings account program run by the Bank of North Dakota for students not in public school or homeschool, depositing 10% to 35% of the state per-pupil payment by household income, and appropriates $21.7 million.

nd:HB 1542.title: AN ACT to create and enact a new section to chapter 44-04 of the North Dakota Century Code, relating to designating student applications for admission to an institution of higher education as exempt records; and to declare an emergency.
nd:HB 1542.summary: Makes records of applications for admission to state-run colleges exempt from open records requirements, and requires them to be destroyed on request of the applicant or, for minors, a parent or guardian.

nd:HB 1575.title: A BILL for an Act to create and enact two new sections to chapter 54-27, two new sections to chapter 57-02, and a new subdivision to subsection 1 of section 57-55-10 of the North Dakota Century Code, relating to a legacy earnings fund, a legacy property tax relief fund, a state reimbursed taxable valuation reduction for residential, agricultural, and commercial property, limitations on taxable valuation increases, and voter-approved excess levy authority; to amend and reenact section 6-09.4-10.1, subsection 1 of section 21-10-06, section 54-27-19.3, subdivision c of subsection 1 of section 57-02-08.1, subdivision b of subsection 2 of section 57-02-08.1, and section 57-02-08.10, of the North Dakota Century Code, relating to funds invested by the state investment board, the homestead tax credit and renters refund, and the primary residence credit certification and state reimbursement; to repeal sections 21-10-12, 21-10-13, and 57-02-08.9 of the North Dakota Century Code, relating to legacy fund definitions, the legacy earnings fund, and the primary residence credit; to provide an appropriation; to provide for a transfer; to provide an effective date; and to provide an expiration date.
nd:HB 1575.summary: Creates a legacy earnings fund fed by a 7% Legacy Fund draw. Cuts taxable valuation by 2.75% of assessed value for residential and 1.5% for agricultural and commercial property, with state reimbursement, caps yearly increases at 3%, and requires voter approval of excess levies.

nd:HB 1580.title: AN ACT to provide for a legislative management study relating to state employee compensation levels.
nd:HB 1580.summary: Directs the Legislative Management to consider studying state employee pay grades, classifications, health benefits and premiums, including comparisons with private sector jobs.

nd:HB 1581.title: AN ACT to provide an appropriation to the department of commerce for tribal tourism grants; and to provide for a legislative management report.
nd:HB 1581.summary: Appropriates $100,000 to the Department of Commerce for grants of up to $20,000 to tribal governments, matching their own funds, to promote tribal tourism.

nd:HB 1582.title: AN ACT to provide for a legislative management study regarding a review of state laws relating to false accusations or false reports of a crime.
nd:HB 1582.summary: Directs the Legislative Management to consider studying the state's laws on false accusations and false reports of a crime, with input from state's attorneys and defense attorneys.

nd:HB 1600.title: AN ACT to create and enact a new section to chapter 15-11 of the North Dakota Century Code, relating to the establishment of the immigration law clinic at the university of North Dakota school of law; to provide for a report; and to provide an appropriation.
nd:HB 1600.summary: Requires the University of North Dakota School of Law to employ one full-time attorney for an immigration law clinic, limited to 60 open matters at a time, allows nominal fees, requires a report to the Legislature, and provides funding.

nd:HB 1621.title: AN ACT to amend and reenact subsection 1 of section 15.1-21-01 and section 15.1-21-02 of the North Dakota Century Code, relating to requiring the presidential physical fitness test in physical education courses in elementary, middle, and high schools and providing exceptions to the test; and to provide an effective date.
nd:HB 1621.summary: Requires physical education courses in elementary, middle and high schools to include participation in the presidential physical fitness test, and lets the Superintendent of Public Instruction set exceptions.

nd:HB 1624.title: A BILL for an Act to create and enact two new sections to chapter 15.1-07 of the North Dakota Century Code, relating to offering school breakfast and lunch at no cost and the school meals fund; to provide an appropriation; to provide for a transfer; and to provide an effective date.
nd:HB 1624.summary: Requires public schools to provide one breakfast and one lunch daily at no cost to any student who asks, with the state reimbursing the gap between federal reimbursement rates and amounts actually received.

nd:HB 1626.title: AN ACT to amend and reenact subdivision d of subsection 1 of section 57-02-08.9, section 57-20-09, and subsection 1 of section 57-55-03 of the North Dakota Century Code, relating to application of the primary residence credit and discount for early payment of tax; and to provide an effective date.
nd:HB 1626.summary: Requires the primary residence property tax credit to be applied after the early-payment discount, with matching changes for real estate and mobile home taxes.

nd:SB 2002.title: AN ACT to provide an appropriation for defraying the expenses of the judicial branch; to provide an appropriation to the office of guardianship and conservatorship; to create and enact a new subsection to section 54-06-08.2 of the North Dakota Century Code, relating to credit and debit card fees; to amend and reenact sections 27-02-02 and 27-05-03 of the North Dakota Century Code, relating to the salaries of justices of the supreme court and salaries of district court judges; to provide for transfers; to provide for a report; and to provide an exemption.
nd:SB 2002.summary: Appropriates money to the judicial branch and the Office of Guardianship and Conservatorship for 2025-27 and changes salaries for supreme court justices and district court judges.

nd:SB 2004.title: AN ACT to provide an appropriation for defraying the expenses of the ethics commission; to create and enact a new section to chapter 54-03 and two new sections to chapter 54-66 of the North Dakota Century Code, relating to immunity and a defense for individuals voting on legislation, closure of a matter of the ethics commission, rules for complaint management time standards, and an ethics commission annual report; to amend and reenact sections 12.1-13-02, 54-66-01, 54-66-04, 54-66-05, 54-66-06, and 54-66-07, subsection 2 of section 54-66-08, and sections 54-66-09, 54-66-10, 54-66-12, and 54-66-18 of the North Dakota Century Code, relating to immunity from criminal prosecution, definitions, ethics commission meetings, complaints, an informal resolution process, law enforcement referrals, findings, appeals, confidential information related to a complaint, and conflicts of interest; and to declare an emergency.
nd:SB 2004.summary: Appropriates money to the Ethics Commission for 2025-27 and changes ethics law, including immunity and a defense for people voting on legislation, closure of commission matters, complaint time standards and an annual report.

nd:SB 2009.title: AN ACT to provide an appropriation for defraying the expenses of the state fair association; to repeal section 4.1-45-22.1 of the North Dakota Century Code, relating to state fair facility operations and maintenance costs; and to declare an emergency.
nd:SB 2009.summary: Appropriates about $2.2 million to the State Fair Association for 2025-27, including campground rest facility funding, and repeals the state fair facility operations and maintenance cost provision.

nd:SB 2014.title: AN ACT to provide an appropriation for defraying the expenses of the industrial commission and the agencies under its control; to create and enact a new section to chapter 6-09 and a new subdivision to subsection 2 of section 38-08-04.5 of the North Dakota Century Code, relating to a rail revolving loan fund and uses of the abandoned oil and gas well plugging and site reclamation fund; to amend and reenact subsection 7 of section 6-08.1-02 and sections 6-09-35, 6-09-46.2, 6-09.7-05, 6-09.14-04, and 49-17.1-02.1, subsection 1 of section 54-17-40, and subdivision a of subsection 4 of section 54-17.7-04 of the North Dakota Century Code, and section 15 of chapter 14 of the 2023 Session Laws, relating to confidential and exempt records of the Bank of North Dakota, the rebuilders loan program, loan guarantees through the strategic investment and improvements fund, interest rate buydown limits for the partnership in assisting community expansion fund, department of transportation review and approval of rail projects, uses of the housing incentive fund, North Dakota pipeline borrowing authority, and a salt cavern underground energy storage research project; to repeal section 3 of Senate Bill No. 2188, as approved by the sixty-ninth legislative assembly, relating to a transfer from the strategic investment and improvements fund to the clean sustainable energy fund; to provide a deficiency appropriation; to provide for a transfer; to provide an exemption; to provide for a legislative management study; to provide for a legislative management report; to provide for a report; to provide an effective date; and to declare an emergency.
nd:SB 2014.summary: Appropriates about $439 million to the Industrial Commission and the agencies it controls for 2025-27, creates a rail revolving loan fund, and sets uses for the abandoned oil and gas well plugging and site reclamation fund.

nd:SB 2018.title: AN ACT to provide an appropriation for defraying the expenses of the department of commerce; to provide an appropriation to the attorney general; to provide an appropriation to the department of career and technical education; to provide an appropriation to the state fair association; to provide a contingent appropriation; to create and enact a new section to chapter 54-60 of the North Dakota Century Code, relating to department of commerce grant reporting requirements; to amend and reenact subsection 1 of section 10-30.5-02, sections 54-60-09, 54-60-19, 54-60-28, 54-60-29, 54-60-29.1, and 54-60-31 of the North Dakota Century Code, relating to the purpose of the North Dakota development fund, duties and talent strategy of the division of workforce development, the uncrewed aircraft systems program, the uncrewed aircraft systems program fund, the beyond visual line of sight uncrewed aircraft system program, and changing the name of the office of legal immigration to the global talent office; to authorize a Bank of North Dakota line of credit; to provide for a transfer; to provide an application; to provide an exemption; and to provide for a legislative management report.
nd:SB 2018.summary: Appropriates about $158 million to the Department of Commerce for 2025-27, plus money for the Attorney General, career and technical education and the State Fair, and requires Commerce to report on grants.

nd:SB 2020.title: AN ACT to provide an appropriation for defraying the expenses of the North Dakota state university extension service, northern crops institute, upper great plains transportation institute, main research center, branch research centers, and agronomy seed farm; to provide for a report; to provide an exemption; and to declare an emergency.
nd:SB 2020.summary: Appropriates money for 2025-27 to the NDSU Extension Service, Northern Crops Institute, Upper Great Plains Transportation Institute, main research center, branch research centers and the agronomy seed farm.

nd:SB 2029.title: AN ACT to create and enact a new subsection to section 30.1-28-07 and chapter 54-68 of the North Dakota Century Code, relating to an office of guardianship and conservatorship and the removal of a guardian; to amend and reenact section 30.1-29-15 and subsection 1 of section 50-24.1-07 of the North Dakota Century Code, relating to the removal of a conservator and the recovery of medical assistance expenses; to repeal chapter 27-27 and section 54-68-02.1 of the North Dakota Century Code, relating to the task force on guardianship monitoring and transition requirements; to provide a penalty; to provide for a report; to provide an appropriation; to provide a continuing appropriation; to provide for a transfer; and to provide an effective date.
nd:SB 2029.summary: Creates a state Office of Guardianship and Conservatorship, lets courts add guardians removed for good cause to a registry that disqualifies them, and repeals the guardianship monitoring task force.

nd:SB 2093.title: A BILL for an Act to amend and reenact subdivision u of subsection 2 of section 57-38-30.3 of the North Dakota Century Code, relating to an income tax deduction for retired law enforcement personnel benefits; and to provide for retroactive application.
nd:SB 2093.summary: Sets income tax rate schedules with 0%, 1.95% and 2.5% brackets for individuals, estates and trusts starting with tax year 2025, and changes the retired peace officer benefits deduction retroactive to tax year 2024.

nd:SB 2113.title: AN ACT to create and enact two new sections to chapter 50-06 of the North Dakota Century Code, relating to certified community behavioral health clinics and the financing of health and human services; to amend and reenact section 12.1-04-06, subsection 4 of section 20.1-03-04, sections 25-03.1-03.1 and 25-03.1-04, subsection 3 of section 25-03.1-08, section 25-03.1-10, subsection 3 of section 25-03.1-11, subsection 1 of section 25-03.1-19, subsection 2 of section 25-03.1-26, subdivision b of subsection 2 of section 26.1-36-08, subdivisions c and d of subsection 2 of section 26.1-36-09, subsection 9 of section 43-12.1-04, subsection 6 of section 43-41-02, subdivision b of subsection 1 of section 44-04-18.30, sections 50-06-01, 50-06-01.4, 50-06-01.7, 50-06-05.1, 50-06-05.2, 50-06-05.3, 50-06-05.4, 50-06-05.5, 50-06-06.2, 50-06-06.5, and 50-06-06.13, subsections 1 and 3 of section 50-06-15, sections 50-06-33 and 50-06-41.3, subsection 1 of section 50-06-42, subsection 1 of section 50-06-42.1, and sections 50-06-46, 50-06.2-01, 50-06.2-02, 50-06.2-03, 50-06.3-02, and 50-06.3-04 of the North Dakota Century Code, relating to the powers and duties of the department of health and human services, treatment hearing timelines, and membership of the cross-disability advisory council; to provide for a legislative management study; and to provide an expiration date.
nd:SB 2113.summary: Requires state certification of certified community behavioral health clinics, creates a health and human services operating special fund, and changes behavioral health and commitment laws, including replacing human service centers with state-operated behavioral health clinics.

nd:SB 2188.title: AN ACT to amend and reenact sections 54-63.1-03 and 54-63.1-07 of the North Dakota Century Code, relating to the membership of the clean sustainable energy authority and the clean sustainable energy fund line of credit; and to provide for a transfer.
nd:SB 2188.summary: Changes the membership of the Clean Sustainable Energy Authority to 18 members, nine voting and nine nonvoting advisors, and changes its fund line of credit.

nd:SB 2213.title: AN ACT to create and enact a new section to chapter 15.1-13 and two new sections to chapter 15.1-21 of the North Dakota Century Code, relating to mathematics curriculum, professional development, screening and intervention, related administrative rules and reporting requirements, and mathematics instructor competency; to provide for a legislative management report; to provide for a department of public instruction mathematics screening pilot program; to provide an appropriation; and to provide an effective date.
nd:SB 2213.summary: Requires teaching candidates for elementary and secondary math to show competence in explicit math instruction, and sets math curriculum, professional development and screening requirements, a screening pilot program and a funding appropriation.

nd:SB 2225.title: A BILL for an Act to provide an appropriation to the department of commerce for a housing for opportunity, mobility, and empowerment program; to provide for a legislative management report; and to declare an emergency.
nd:SB 2225.summary: Appropriates $25 million from the strategic investment and improvements fund to the Department of Commerce for grants to local governments to build infrastructure for affordable and market-rate housing, with a legislative report.

nd:SB 2308.title: AN ACT to create and enact a new section to chapter 23.1-01, a new section to chapter 54-07, and two new sections to chapter 61-03 of the North Dakota Century Code, relating to standards for well drilling and installation of water well pumps, pitless units, and monitoring wells, a boards review task force, a water well contractors advisory board, and requirements for firms engaged in water well work, installation of water well pump and pitless units, monitoring well work, and drilling of geothermal systems; to amend and reenact section 6-09-43, subdivision j of subsection 2 of section 15.1-01-04, sections 15.1-07-33 and 23-35-02.2, subsection 1 of section 50-06-01.4, sections 52-02-02 and 52-02-08, subsection 1 of section 54-07-01.2, sections 54-54-05, 54-59-26, 54-59-27, 54-59-34, 54-59-36, 54-59-37, 54-59-39, 61-03-01.3, 61-04.1-03, 61-04.1-08, 61-04.1-09, 61-04.1-12, 61-04.1-14, 61-04.1-15, 61-04.1-16, 61-04.1-17, 61-04.1-18, 61-04.1-19, 61-04.1-20, 61-04.1-21, 61-04.1-33, 61-04.1-34, 61-04.1-37, 61-04.1-38, and 61-04.1-39, and subdivision a of subsection 2 of section 65-02-03.1 of the North Dakota Century Code, relating to the wastewater recycling treatment guide, boards and commissions, the unemployment insurance advisory council, gubernatorial appointments, the committee on aging, health information technology advisory committee, statewide longitudinal data system committee, atmospheric resource board, the department of health and human services, the council on the arts, the state engineer, the superintendent of public instruction, job service North Dakota, and workforce safety and insurance coordinating committee; to repeal chapter 8-11.1, sections 12-48-06.1, 15.1-37-05, 15.1-37-06, and 15.1-37-08, chapter 17-07, sections 19-24.1-38, 19-24.1-39, and 23-35-02.3, chapters 34-16 and 43-35, sections 50-06-05.6, 50-06.4-10, 50-11.1-25, 50-11.1-26, 50-11.1-27, 52-02-07, 54-34.3-10, 54-54-10, 54-59-25, 54-59-33, 54-59-35, 54-59-38, 54-60-25, 55-01-13, 55-01-14, 61-04.1-04, 61-04.1-05, 61-04.1-06, 61-04.1-07, and 61-04.1-10, and chapter 61-36 of the North Dakota Century Code, relating to occupational and professional boards, the midwest interstate passenger rail compact, prison industry advisory committee, energy policy commission, medical marijuana advisory committee, onsite wastewater recycling technical committee, state board of water well contractors, committee on aging, brain injury advisory council, early childhood council, unemployment insurance advisory council, commission on the status of women, health information technology advisory committee, poet laureate nominating board, rural development council, America 250 commission, atmospheric resource board, and Devils Lake outlet management advisory committee; to provide for a legislative management report; to provide an effective date; and to provide an expiration date.
nd:SB 2308.summary: Repeals statutes for a number of state boards and committees, creates a boards review task force and a water well contractors advisory board, and sets requirements for firms doing water well work.

nd:SB 2354.title: AN ACT to amend and reenact the new section to chapter 15.1-07 of the North Dakota Century Code, as created by House Bill No. 1160, as approved by the sixty-ninth legislative assembly, relating to the use of personal electronic devices in schools providing prekindergarten, elementary, or secondary education.
nd:SB 2354.summary: Amends the school phone law: devices must be turned off, stowed away and inaccessible during instructional time, medical and individualized-plan exceptions remain, and districts must communicate the policy and publish it in handbooks.

nd:SB 2390.title: AN ACT to create and enact three new sections to chapter 54-40.1 of the North Dakota Century Code, relating to a rural catalyst committee, grant program, and fund; to amend and reenact section 54-40.1-02 of the North Dakota Century Code, relating to definitions for regional planning councils; to provide an appropriation; and to provide for a transfer.
nd:SB 2390.summary: Creates a rural catalyst committee, grant program and fund through the Department of Commerce, with grants requiring at least a dollar of non-state matching funds for each state dollar.

nd:SB 2397.title: AN ACT to create and enact a new subsection to section 57-51.1-03 of the North Dakota Century Code, relating to a limited exemption for development incentive wells; to amend and reenact sections 57-51-02.6, 57-51-05, and 57-51.1-01 of the North Dakota Century Code, relating to the temporary exemption for oil and gas wells employing a system to avoid flaring, an exemption from gross production tax for gas produced from certain enhanced oil recovery projects, and the definition of development incentive well; to provide an effective date; and to provide an expiration date.
nd:SB 2397.summary: Changes oil and gas tax exemptions, including the temporary exemption for wells that avoid flaring, an exemption from gross production tax for gas from certain enhanced oil recovery projects, and a limited exemption for development incentive wells.

nd:SB 2399.title: AN ACT to create and enact a new section to chapter 50-24.1 of the North Dakota Century Code, relating to medical assistance reimbursement of psychiatric residential treatment facilities; to provide for a legislative management report; and to provide an appropriation.
nd:SB 2399.summary: Directs the Department of Health and Human Services to amend Medicaid reimbursement rules for psychiatric residential treatment facilities' direct care costs, capping therapeutic leave days at $500 per day, and to report by October 1, 2026.

nd:SB 2401.title: AN ACT to create and enact a new subdivision to subsection 2 of section 12-60-24 of the North Dakota Century Code, relating to criminal history record checks by the board of occupational therapy practice; to amend and reenact section 43-17-27.1 of the North Dakota Century Code, relating to physician continuing education requirements; to provide a statement of legislative intent; and to provide an effective date.
nd:SB 2401.summary: Allows the Board of Occupational Therapy Practice to run criminal history record checks on applicants and licensees, and requires physicians to complete at least one hour of continuing education on nutrition and metabolic health each renewal cycle.

nd:SB 2405.title: A BILL for an Act to amend and reenact subsection 1 of section 57-02-08.9, section 57-20-09, and subsection 1 of section 57-55-03 of the North Dakota Century Code, relating to the order of application of the primary residence credit and discount for early payment of tax; and to provide an effective date.
nd:SB 2405.summary: Requires the primary residence property tax credit to be applied after the 5% early-payment discount, rather than before it.

nd:SB 2406.title: A BILL for an Act to create and enact chapter 44-04.1 of the North Dakota Century Code, relating to prohibiting agencies from entering nondisclosure agreements concerning data centers and industrial projects; to provide a penalty; to provide an effective date; and to provide an expiration date.
nd:SB 2406.summary: Bars state and local agencies from signing nondisclosure agreements with developers of data centers and industrial projects, voids such agreements, and bars approvals of projects whose developer signed one.

nd:SB 2407.title: AN ACT to provide an appropriation to the state historical society for the North Dakota military museum project; to amend and reenact section 55-01-02.1 of the North Dakota Century Code, relating to jurisdiction of the heritage center; to repeal subsection 3 of section 6 of chapter 17 of the 2025 Session Laws, relating to a donation pledge requirement to access funding from the strategic investment and improvements fund; to provide a statement of legislative intent; to authorize a line of credit; to provide for a report; and to provide an effective date.
nd:SB 2407.summary: Allows the State Historical Society to borrow up to $20 million from the Bank of North Dakota for the military museum project through June 30, 2027, and repeals a donation pledge requirement for related state funding.

nd:SB 2408.title: A BILL for an Act to create and enact subdivision lll of subsection 3 of section 19-03.1-05 of the North Dakota Century Code, relating to the scheduling of kratom alkaloids and kratom alkaloid derivatives as a schedule I controlled substance; to amend and reenact section 19-03.1-22.3 and subsection 7 of section 19-03.1-23 of the North Dakota Century Code, relating to penalties for the use and possession of kratom alkaloids and kratom alkaloid derivatives; to provide a penalty; and to provide an effective date.
nd:SB 2408.summary: Lists kratom alkaloids and their derivatives as schedule I controlled substances and makes ingesting them an infraction for a first offense and a class A misdemeanor for later offenses.

tn:HB 1572.title: Sunset Laws - As enacted, extends the department of children's services to June 30, 2028; requires the department to report back to the government operations committee by December 31, 2026, to update the committee on its progress in addressing the findings and observations set forth in the December 2025 performance audit report. - Amends TCA Title 4, Chapter 29 and Title 37, Chapter 5.
tn:HB 1572.summary: Extends the Department of Children's Services' termination date to June 30, 2028, and requires it to report to a legislative committee by December 31, 2026 on its progress addressing the December 2025 state audit findings.

tn:HB 1652.title: Alcoholic Beverages - As enacted, establishes new premier type tourist resorts, restaurants, community theaters, clubs, retirement centers, premises, and commercial passenger boat companies that can offer liquor by the  drink; makes related changes. - Amends TCA Title 57.
tn:HB 1652.summary: Adds definitions of specific community theaters, recreational clubs, social clubs, marinas and other facilities, described by size, features and local population, so they can be licensed to serve liquor by the drink.

tn:HB 1667.title: Local Government, General - As enacted, authorizes municipalities and metropolitan governments to adopt a tiered system of monetary penalties for repeated violations of the same municipal ordinance by the same person or entity within a 12-month period. - Amends TCA Title 6 and Title 7.
tn:HB 1667.summary: Lets home rule cities, other municipalities and metropolitan governments set, by ordinance, tiered fines that increase for repeat violations of the same ordinance by the same person or entity within 12 months, starting July 1, 2026.

tn:HB 1802.title: Firearms and Ammunition - As enacted, lowers the standard for the use of deadly force to protect property. - Amends TCA Title 39.
tn:HB 1802.summary: Allows a person lawfully residing in a place, and not committing a felony or Class A misdemeanor, to use deadly force to protect property from imminent arson, burglary, robbery or aggravated animal cruelty when no other means work and death or serious injury is imminent.

tn:HB 2196.title: Local Government, General - As enacted, authorizes Putnam County and incorporated cities within the county to regulate sober living homes for recovery from alcohol, drug, and substance abuse to the extent such regulation complies with the Fair Housing Act and the Americans with Disabilities Act. - Amends TCA Title 7, Chapter 51, Part 26.
tn:HB 2196.summary: Changes the definition of 'local government' for regulating sober living homes to counties, and cities within them, with 2020 census populations of 366,200-366,300 or 79,800-79,900.

tn:HB 2290.title: Hospitals and Health Care Facilities - As enacted, requires each fertility clinic operating in this state to obtain a certificate from the department of health to perform assisted reproductive technology services. - Amends TCA Title 4; Title 29; Title 36; Title 63 and Title 68.
tn:HB 2290.summary: Requires each fertility clinic to hold a state health department certificate, renewed every two years, showing professional-society membership, an embryo transfer plan if it closes, and a passed lab inspection. Sets qualifications for clinical directors.

tn:HB 2476.title: Public Funds and Financing - As enacted, revises law relative to pension plans and proxy advisors. - Amends TCA Title 9, Chapter 4.
tn:HB 2476.summary: Requires local governments with pension plans to invest and vote shares for financial reasons, file an annual proxy-advisor report by September 1, and bars proxy advisory firms with conflicts of interest from advising those plans.

tn:HB 2616.title: Open Meetings - As enacted, authorizes a governing body to conduct an executive session for the purpose of interviewing applicants for employment as director-level staff of the body without providing public notice of such session. - Amends TCA Title 8.
tn:HB 2616.summary: Allows a governing body to hold a closed executive session, without public notice, to interview applicants for director-level staff jobs. Deliberation and votes must occur in an open, noticed meeting.

tn:HB 794.title: Utilities, Utility Districts - As enacted, establishes a process for a municipality that operates a sewerage system outside of its corporate boundaries and has imposed a moratorium on new sewer connections outside of its corporate boundaries for a period of five or more consecutive years to extend sanitary sewer service or allow sewer connection only to property located within an adjacency area if the property owner or developer agrees to pay, or the municipality assesses, a housing surcharge. - Amends TCA Title 4; Title 5; Title 6; Title 7; Title 8; Title 12; Title 13; Title 29; Title 54; Title 64; Title 65; Title 68 and Title 69.
tn:HB 794.summary: Lets a city with a sewer moratorium outside its limits lasting five or more years connect only adjacent properties, if owners pay a housing surcharge. Surcharge goes to an affordable housing fund and is capped at 3% of appraised value for single-family lots.

tn:SB 1232.title: Courts - As enacted, enacts the "Recovery Court Renewal Act." - Amends TCA Title 40, Chapter 32, Part 1.
tn:SB 1232.summary: Allows expunction of an offense committed at least ten years after a DUI conviction, for a person with one DUI conviction who completed a recovery court program and sentence and has no prior expunction. Excludes offenses involving a vehicle and alcohol or drugs.

tn:SB 1326.title: Taxes, Real Property - As enacted, provides that a collecting official or the division of property assessments is not required to request documentation verifying the income of an elderly person seeking tax relief if the applicant is at least 80 years old and meets certain other requirements. - Amends TCA Title 67, Chapter 5, Part 7.
tn:SB 1326.summary: Lets property tax relief applicants aged 80 or older skip income documentation if they received relief the prior five years and income is under the limit. Requires annual reapplication through a simplified form.

tn:SB 1874.title: Unemployment Compensation - As enacted, removes a requirement that work be deemed suitable for a claimant if certain criteria are met and a claimant's gross weekly wages equal or exceed certain threshold percentages of the claimant's weekly wage for insured work for the quarter of the base period when the claimant's wages were greatest. - Amends TCA Section 50-7-303.
tn:SB 1874.summary: Repeals the wage-percentage tests under which new work counts as suitable for an unemployment claimant based on its pay compared with the claimant's earlier wages.

tn:SB 2162.title: Open Meetings - As enacted, authorizes a governing body to conduct an executive session for the purpose of interviewing applicants for employment as director-level staff of the body without providing public notice of such session. - Amends TCA Title 8.
tn:SB 2162.summary: Allows a governing body to hold a closed executive session, without public notice, to interview applicants for director-level staff jobs. Deliberation and votes must occur in an open, noticed meeting.

tn:SB 2213.title: Public Utilities - As enacted, requires a utility to provide material that is required for construction of utility infrastructure for the customer's or approved contractor's use at the same price as the utility paid for the material, if such material is available only from the utility; authorizes a customer or approved contractor installing utility infrastructure to install street lights; prohibits a utility from requiring a customer or approved contractor from installing street lights; prohibits certain fees for inspections and review of plans and designs from exceeding a combined total of 10% of the proposed cost of the project. - Amends TCA Title 7; Title 13, Chapter 7; Title 65 and Title 68.
tn:SB 2213.summary: Requires a utility to sell required construction materials available only from it at the price it paid, bars requiring customers to install street lights, and caps plan review and inspection fees at 10% of project cost.

tn:SB 2237.title: Local Government, General - As enacted, requires a local government responsible for reviewing a development application, development plan, or a site inspection submitted by a developer for the purpose of developing real property in this state, within 60 business days of the submission, to approve the application, plan, or site inspection or add the submission to the next available agenda of either the planning commission or the governing body; makes other related changes. - Amends TCA Title 7.
tn:SB 2237.summary: Requires a local government to approve a development application or place it on an agenda within 60 business days, or send a deficiency report or information request within 30. If it takes no action, the submission is deemed approved.

tn:SB 2317.title: Education - As enacted, requires the department of education to implement a pilot program to evaluate whether administering fewer district- and state-mandated assessments results in students achieving greater academic success; adds an additional method by which a student who is not proficient in ELA, as determined by the student's achieving a performance level rating of “approaching” on the ELA portion of the student's most recent TCAP test, may be promoted. - Amends TCA Title 49.
tn:SB 2317.summary: Requires the Department of Education to run a pilot with up to ten school districts testing whether fewer state and district assessments help students, limiting tests for K-8 students above the 40th percentile on screeners in 2027-2029.

tn:SB 254.title: Criminal Procedure - As enacted, requires a defendant who is ordered to wear a transdermal monitoring device or alternative device, including other alternative alcohol or drug monitoring device, or global positioning monitoring device, as a condition of pretrial release, and who has not been determined by the court to be indigent, to pay all fees associated with the installation, monitoring, maintenance, and operation of the device. - Amends TCA Title 38; Title 39; Title 40 and Title 55.
tn:SB 254.summary: Requires a defendant not found indigent who must wear an alcohol or drug monitoring device as a condition of pretrial release or probation to pay its fees. Nonpayment can lead to a show cause hearing, possible bond revocation, or end of monitoring.

tn:SB 2557.title: Insurance, Health, Accident - As enacted, authorizes a health insurance entity to offer a short-term limited-duration plan and hospital indemnity coverage on the marketplace. - Amends TCA Title 3; Title 4; Title 5; Title 6; Title 7; Title 8; Title 10; Title 12; Title 29; Title 35; Title 36; Title 37; Title 39; Title 40; Title 41; Title 42; Title 45; Title 47; Title 49; Title 50; Title 52; Title 53; Title 56; Title 58; Title 63; Title 67; Title 68 and Title 71.
tn:SB 2557.summary: Allows health insurers to offer short-term limited-duration plans, with a deductible up to $10,000 and a $1 million per-person benefit cap, and hospital indemnity coverage on Tennessee's federal insurance marketplace.

tn:SB 2646.title: Industrial Development - As enacted, revises law relative to industrial development corporations. - Amends TCA Title 7 and Title 48.
tn:SB 2646.summary: Lets an industrial development board initiate a merger, and changes who must approve payments in lieu of taxes: letters of support or notice to local chief executives, with legislative approval required in some cases.

tn:SB 879.title: Human Services, Dept. of - As enacted, requires the commissioner to provide the commissioner of correction with a form application for food assistance for use by inmates who are preparing for release. - Amends TCA Title 71, Chapter 5, Part 3.
tn:SB 879.summary: Requires the human services commissioner to give the correction commissioner a food assistance application for inmates preparing for release, with an option to decline. Requires prisons to distribute and collect forms and report annually.

tx:HB 1.title: Relating to youth camp emergency plans and preparedness; authorizing penalties.
tx:HB 1.summary: Requires resident youth camp operators to write, annually review, and train staff on emergency plans, give copies to local emergency officials, and submit to state health department review. Allows the attorney general to seek civil penalties.

tx:HB 18.title: Relating to a restriction on the acceptance of political contributions and the making of certain political expenditures by a member of the legislature and certain political committees during certain periods in which a member is absent from a legislative session; authorizing a civil penalty.
tx:HB 18.summary: Bars a legislator, and committees or caucuses supporting them, from accepting contributions above the legislative per diem or paying travel, food or lodging expenses during an absence that impedes a legislative session. Sets a civil penalty up to $5,000.

tx:HB 22.title: Relating to the authority of the comptroller to provide funding for the deployment and operation of certain emergency communication equipment.
tx:HB 22.summary: Expands uses of the state broadband infrastructure fund to pay for early warning and emergency notification systems and interoperable emergency communication equipment, including operating costs.

tx:HB 23.title: Relating to the exemption from ad valorem taxation of property owned by certain nonprofit corporations, located in a populous county, and used to promote agriculture, support youth, and provide educational support in the community.
tx:HB 23.summary: Exempts from property tax real and personal property owned by certain nonprofits in counties of 3.3 million or more that promote agriculture, support youth and provide educational support.

tx:HB 25.title: Relating to a pharmacist's authority to dispense ivermectin without a prescription.
tx:HB 25.summary: Allows pharmacists to dispense ivermectin without a prescription under Board of Pharmacy protocols, shields a pharmacist acting in a reasonably prudent manner from criminal liability and professional discipline, and lets the Texas State Board of Pharmacy adopt rules.

tx:HB 26.title: Relating to contracting with law enforcement agencies in certain counties.
tx:HB 26.summary: Allows sheriffs and constables in counties of more than 3.3 million people to contract with local governments, property owners' associations or landowners to provide law enforcement services, without county commissioners court approval.

tx:HB 27.title: Relating to a groundwater study of certain aquifers underlying the territory of the Neches and Trinity Valleys Groundwater Conservation District by the Texas Water Development Board before the issuance of permits or permit amendments by the district.
tx:HB 27.summary: Requires the Texas Water Development Board to study the effects of groundwater pumping on aquifers under the Neches and Trinity Valleys district and report. Pauses new district permits to produce and export groundwater until 270 days after the report is due.

tx:HB 4.title: Relating to the composition of the districts for the election of members of the United States House of Representatives from the State of Texas.
tx:HB 4.summary: Adopts a new map of Texas's U.S. House districts, designated plan PLANC2333, with one member elected from each district.

tx:HB 7.title: Relating to prohibitions on the manufacture and provision of abortion-inducing drugs, including the jurisdiction of and effect of certain judgments by courts within and outside this state with respect to the manufacture and provision of those drugs, and to protections from certain counteractions under the laws of other states and jurisdictions; authorizing qui tam actions.
tx:HB 7.summary: Bars manufacturing, distributing, mailing or prescribing abortion-inducing drugs in or into Texas. Enforced only through private qui tam lawsuits.

tx:HB 8.title: Relating to public school accountability and transparency, including the implementation of an instructionally supportive assessment program and the adoption and administration of assessment instruments in public schools, indicators of achievement, public school performance ratings, and interventions and sanctions under the public school accountability system, a grant program for school district local accountability plans, and actions challenging Texas Education Agency decisions related to public school accountability.
tx:HB 8.summary: Replaces the state's public school testing program with an instructionally supportive assessment program run by the Texas Education Agency, changes how school performance ratings are set, and allows legal challenges to agency accountability decisions.

tx:HR 128.title: Amending the House Rules of Procedure to authorize additional constitutionally compliant, proportional penalties for members absent without leave for purpose of impeding the action of the House that do not unfairly impair members' representative functions.
tx:HR 128.summary: As introduced, amends House rules to set penalties for members absent without leave to block House action, including fines, loss of committee chair posts, and reduced seniority, unless the House excuses them by majority vote.

tx:HR 174.title: Suspending limitations on conference committee jurisdiction, S.B. No. 5.
tx:HR 174.summary: Suspends House rules so the conference committee on Senate Bill 5 can add contingent funding for the Department of State Health Services for campground and youth camp safety ($2.59 million from the stabilization fund, $2.48 million from general revenue) and make the act effective immediately.

tx:SB 1.title: Relating to campground and youth camp safety.
tx:SB 1.summary: Sets safety rules for campgrounds and youth camps, including emergency plans and rooftop ladders in floodplain cabins. Bars youth camps from operating cabins in a floodplain, and requires weather alert radios, warning systems and camper accounting procedures.

tx:SB 10.title: Relating to the calculation of the voter-approval tax rate for certain taxing units.
tx:SB 10.summary: Lowers from 1.035 to 1.025 the multiplier used to calculate the voter-approval property tax rate for most taxing units, other than special taxing units and counties or cities under 75,000 people, starting January 1, 2026.

tx:SB 12.title: Relating to the duty of the attorney general to prosecute criminal offenses prescribed by the election laws of this state.
tx:SB 12.summary: Requires the attorney general to prosecute election-law crimes, requires local law enforcement to send probable-cause reports to the attorney general as well, and requires local prosecutors to hand over investigation information on request.

tx:SB 14.title: Relating to the provision by a political subdivision of credits against impact fees to builders and developers for certain water conservation and reuse projects.
tx:SB 14.summary: Requires cities and other political subdivisions to give builders and developers a credit against water and wastewater impact fees for facilities, systems or products that conserve or reuse water.

tx:SB 8.title: Relating to the designation and use of certain spaces and facilities according to sex; authorizing a civil penalty and a private civil right of action.
tx:SB 8.summary: Requires state agencies and local governments to designate multiple-occupancy restrooms, locker rooms and similar spaces in their buildings for one sex only and take reasonable steps to keep others out. Creates a civil penalty and private lawsuit right, and sets sex-based housing for prisons.

ut:HB 101.title: Firearm Background Check Amendments
ut:HB 101.summary: Exempts a buyer from a firearm background check for a National Firearms Act firearm if ATF approved the transfer application within the last 30 days, and clarifies that licensed dealers need no background check for transfers to a dealer.

ut:HB 102.title: Victim Privacy Amendments
ut:HB 102.summary: Lets a crime victim request that initials replace the victim's name in publicly available criminal justice documents, while requiring entities to give the name in response to a court order.

ut:HB 110.title: Offender Modifications
ut:HB 110.summary: Lets courts order Adult Probation and Parole to supervise class B misdemeanants it agrees to supervise, adds parole-board considerations after revoked paroles, and sets waiting periods of 10 or 20 years before pardon consideration for registered sex offenders.

ut:HB 111.title: Wildlife Amendments
ut:HB 111.summary: Changes wildlife laws, including creating a Poaching Mitigation Fund from restitution money, providing for grizzly bear management, and changing definitions, fees and limits for guides and outfitters.

ut:HB 113.title: Emergency Reporting Abuse Amendments
ut:HB 113.summary: Expands the offense of emergency reporting abuse to cover contacting 911 when the caller knows or should know no emergency or crime exists, and adds new penalties.

ut:HB 118.title: Driver Training Schools for Commercial Driver License Amendments
ut:HB 118.summary: Requires commercial driver license applicants to sign a form attesting to their English language ability, and requires reporting on commercial driver training schools.

ut:HB 122.title: Pregnant and Postpartum Inmate Amendments
ut:HB 122.summary: Requires prisons and jails to report numbers of pregnant inmates and inmate parents, sets a 12-week postpartum period, bars restraints then without an individualized security finding, and extends social worker and postpartum care access to 12 weeks.

ut:HB 125.title: Department of Natural Resources Related Modifications Amendments
ut:HB 125.summary: Changes Department of Natural Resources laws on invasive-species rules for boats, water rights records, secondary water metering loans, and the duties and board of the Utah Geological Survey.

ut:HB 128.title: Traffic Amendments
ut:HB 128.summary: Removes the requirement to signal a turn while driving through a roundabout.

ut:HB 136.title: Unlicensed Driver Amendments
ut:HB 136.summary: Changes when police must impound vehicles driven without a valid license, permit or driving privilege card, modifies related fees and penalties, and changes administrative license suspension rules.

ut:HB 137.title: Violent Crime Clearance Rate Amendments
ut:HB 137.summary: Creates the Violent Crime Clearance Rate Fund, administered by the State Commission on Criminal and Juvenile Justice, to award grants to law enforcement agencies for solving violent crimes.

ut:HB 158.title: Unlawful Tracking Amendments
ut:HB 158.summary: Renames and broadens the tracking offense to cover tracking devices placed on personal property and tracking applications, including use after consent is revoked, and requires statutory damages if a victim elects them.

ut:HB 16.title: Solar Power Plant Amendments
ut:HB 16.summary: Sets state incentive eligibility based on land characteristics for utility-scale solar plants, reduces incentives on certain protected farmland, and requires wildlife consultation, decommissioning plans with financial assurance, and a permit process with site plan approval.

ut:HB 178.title: School Zone Speeding Amendments
ut:HB 178.summary: Removes the provision for compensatory service observing a crossing guard as a penalty for a speeding conviction in a school zone.

ut:HB 179.title: Milk Amendments
ut:HB 179.summary: Sets rules for raw milk and raw milk products, including labeling, foodborne illness outbreaks, cease and desist orders, penalties, and an exemption from certain dairy regulations.

ut:HB 185.title: Carbon Credit Amendments
ut:HB 185.summary: Creates the Carbon Credit Litigation Fund, requires state entities that sell or exchange carbon credits to report, and requires the state auditor to report on those sales to a legislative appropriations subcommittee.

ut:HB 187.title: Water Amendments
ut:HB 187.summary: Exempts certain lower-basin water rights of water conservancy districts from abandonment or forfeiture for nonuse and prohibits certain instream flow change applications related to the lower Colorado River basin.

ut:HB 190.title: Child Care Business Tax Credit
ut:HB 190.summary: Expands the employer-provided child care income tax credit to off-site child care facilities, increases the credit for certain small employers, and removes the requirement to have claimed a construction credit first.

ut:HB 192.title: Vehicle Inspection Fee Amendments
ut:HB 192.summary: Removes the statutory cap on labor fees that safety inspection stations may charge and allows a reasonable fee for safety inspections.

ut:HB 195.title: Precious Metals Amendments
ut:HB 195.summary: Requires the state treasurer to continue a precious metals study for two more years and to seek proposals for a precious metals-backed electronic payment system, with annual reports to a legislative committee.

ut:HB 2.title: New Fiscal Year Supplemental Appropriations
ut:HB 2.summary: Adjusts fiscal year 2027 appropriations for state agencies, higher education and other purposes, authorizes full-time employment levels for internal service funds, and includes intent language.

ut:HB 204.title: Higher Education Student Belief Accommodation
ut:HB 204.summary: Broadens the requirement that higher education institutions reasonably accommodate students' sincerely held religious and conscience beliefs, adds notification and review steps, and requires the Board of Higher Education to adopt policies.

ut:HB 209.title: Voting Amendments
ut:HB 209.summary: Creates a process for election officers to determine a voter is not a citizen, and from November 1, 2026 lets voters choose whether to give proof of citizenship; those who do not may vote only in federal races.

ut:HB 214.title: Firearms Liability Amendments
ut:HB 214.summary: Requires courts to dismiss certain lawsuits against firearm sellers, manufacturers and trade associations that fail set requirements, awards defendants attorney fees in some cases, allows interlocutory appeals, and bars local governments from imposing such liability.

ut:HB 220.title: Public Safety Data Amendments
ut:HB 220.summary: Moves several public safety data reports, including on attempted firearm purchases and sexual assaults in detention, from an interim committee to the State Commission on Criminal and Juvenile Justice's public safety portal, and requires colleges to report student housing crime data.

ut:HB 238.title: Utah Energy Generation and Transmission Planning
ut:HB 238.summary: Requires the Public Service Commission to participate in regional transmission organizations where Utah utilities are members, allows it to contract for market analysis, requires annual reports to the Legislature, and requires a simple opt-out for community clean energy programs.

ut:HB 24.title: Criminal Penalty Amendments
ut:HB 24.summary: Reduces speeding 21 to 29 mph in a school zone and careless driving from class C misdemeanors to infractions, and merges the offenses of driving without vehicle security and failing to carry proof of it.

ut:HB 240.title: Carbon Dioxide System Amendments
ut:HB 240.summary: Requires licensing of businesses that service carbon dioxide systems and certification of most individuals who do so, through the state fire marshal, with rules and fees set by the Utah Fire Prevention Board.

ut:HB 243.title: Gambling Revisions
ut:HB 243.summary: Clarifies that a proposition bet falls within the legal definition of gambling.

ut:HB 250.title: Utah Retirement Plan Exchange
ut:HB 250.summary: Directs the state treasurer's office to run a public online exchange where eligible private employers can compare and choose retirement plans, with a listing process for plan providers and annual provider reports.

ut:HB 259.title: Parental Access to Children's Medical Records Amendments
ut:HB 259.summary: Gives parents the right to access a child's medical record, requires health care facilities and electronic record vendors to provide parental access unless exceptions apply, and lets the attorney general bring enforcement actions.

ut:HB 261.title: Electronic Information Privacy Act Amendments
ut:HB 261.summary: Changes rules for law enforcement access to electronic information, makes the act's procedures the only permitted methods, bars using third parties to get data the agency could not get directly, and applies evidence exclusion rules to violations.

ut:HB 269.title: Ambulance Provider Payment Amendments
ut:HB 269.summary: Adjusts Medicaid ambulance rates, lets the Bureau of Emergency Medical Services adjust the base rate yearly, includes medicine costs in the base rate, and repeals sunset dates.

ut:HB 270.title: Healthcare Worker Post-Employment Amendments
ut:HB 270.summary: Makes void non-compete agreements between employers and healthcare workers, and voids certain nonsolicitation agreements between a person and a healthcare worker.

ut:HB 274.title: Sentencing Amendments
ut:HB 274.summary: Changes Sentencing Commission membership, directs it to weigh set objectives and to revise adult guidelines for certain offenses before November 1, 2026, and changes what courts must consider at sentencing.

ut:HB 276.title: Artificial Intelligence Modifications
ut:HB 276.summary: Bars generation services and platforms from distributing counterfeit intimate images without verified consent, creates civil liability, and requires large platforms to preserve content provenance data and AI providers to include disclosures in AI-generated content.

ut:HB 284.title: Murder Offense Amendments
ut:HB 284.summary: Clarifies that murder committed with depraved indifference to human life does not require specific intent to kill a particular person.

ut:HB 290.title: Child Tax Credit Amendments
ut:HB 290.summary: Raises the income thresholds at which the individual income tax credit for child dependents phases out.

ut:HB 291.title: Security and Land Restriction Amendments
ut:HB 291.summary: Lowers the ownership percentage at which an entity counts as a restricted foreign entity, has Public Safety send letters requiring proof within 30 days that an entity is not one, and allows daily fines for nonresponse.

ut:HB 296.title: Water Commitment Amendments
ut:HB 296.summary: Allows a water provider's conservation plan to include a commitment of available water to uses on the Great Salt Lake.

ut:HB 3.title: Appropriations Adjustments
ut:HB 3.summary: Adjusts state appropriations for fiscal years 2026 and 2027, increasing and decreasing budgets for state agencies, public and higher education, and funding bills with fiscal impact passed in the 2026 session.

ut:HB 30.title: Wildlife Management Area Amendments
ut:HB 30.summary: Replaces the hunting or fishing license requirement for wildlife management area access with conditions including an approved educational video, creates a Wildlife Management Area Stewardship Fund, and allows voluntary contributions and volunteer labor.

ut:HB 301.title: Drug Recodification
ut:HB 301.summary: Reorganizes and clarifies Utah laws on drugs, moving certain drug offenses from the occupations and professions title into the criminal code and updating cross references.

ut:HB 303.title: Family Court Amendments
ut:HB 303.summary: Sets factors courts weigh in awarding costs and fees in family law cases, provides a process for ordering mental health treatment in custody cases, and lets courts consider evidence of coercive control in custody and parent-time decisions.

ut:HB 308.title: Homeless Services Amendments
ut:HB 308.summary: Changes homeless services law, including duties of the Office of Homeless Services, letting providers temporarily exceed a congregate shelter's bed limit under conditions, and changing local tax revenue distributions for shelters.

ut:HB 311.title: Elections Study
ut:HB 311.summary: Directs Utah Valley University institutes to study the security of in-person versus mail voting and best practices for requiring ID at ballot drop boxes, and present findings to a legislative committee.

ut:HB 312.title: School Curriculum and Standards Modifications
ut:HB 312.summary: Changes K-12 social studies requirements, including instruction on self-governance and founding documents, splitting civics and U.S. history into two semester courses each, and elementary social studies instruction by July 1, 2031.

ut:HB 313.title: Landscaper Certification Amendments
ut:HB 313.summary: Requires the Division of Professional Licensing to identify a specialty contractor that may do landscape work and sets continuing education requirements for licensees who do landscape work.

ut:HB 314.title: Firearm Purchase Amendments
ut:HB 314.summary: Removes the requirement that licensed firearm dealers use a Bureau of Criminal Identification form for sales and extends how long the bureau may keep background check records from 20 to 30 days.

ut:HB 323.title: Solar Panel Disposal Amendments
