ut:HB 323.summary: Requires solar retailers to disclose solar panel disposal rules, creates a Solar Panel Waste Restricted Account funded by assessments and a distributed generation fee, and from July 1, 2028 allows rules requiring hazardous waste analysis and proper disposal of solar panels.

ut:HB 325.title: Government Records Classification Amendments
ut:HB 325.summary: Classifies as public any record of a government entity's receipt or spending of funds, such as budgets, vouchers, grants and vendor payments, and makes private records that reveal whether a taxpayer receives a property tax exemption or relief.

ut:HB 329.title: State Employee Maternity and Leave Amendments
ut:HB 329.summary: Raises state employee postpartum recovery leave from three to six weeks, adds six weeks of paid leave for adopting a child under six, and creates a separate four-week paid foster leave.

ut:HB 331.title: Criminal Offenses Modifications
ut:HB 331.summary: Renames threat of terrorism as terrorism and extends it to completed acts, and creates offenses of unlawfully advancing foreign organizations and governments, concealing identity while committing an offense in public, and depriving religious rights, with a civil action.

ut:HB 337.title: Nicotine Product Tax Amendments
ut:HB 337.summary: Raises taxes on cigarettes, e-cigarettes and nontherapeutic nicotine devices, replaces weight-based rates on alternative nicotine products with per-pouch or percentage-of-price rates, and imposes a one-time inventory tax on cigarettes.

ut:HB 339.title: Street Medicine Amendments
ut:HB 339.summary: Requires the Department of Health and Human Services to develop a guide for street medicine providers and allows those providers to dispense and administer long-acting injectables.

ut:HB 361.title: Elections Provisions Amendments
ut:HB 361.summary: Changes election procedures, including candidate nickname rules, notice requirements, declaration of candidacy periods, and, from January 1, 2027, barring a county clerk's name from ballots and return envelopes unless the clerk is a candidate.

ut:HB 369.title: Agriculture and Food Amendments
ut:HB 369.summary: Updates Department of Agriculture and Food provisions, including creating a weights and measures account, removing tattoos and the brisket as livestock brand marks and locations, letting the commissioner remove conservation district board members, and repealing farm name registration.

ut:HB 37.title: Used Oil Management Act Amendments
ut:HB 37.summary: Increases the recycling fee on lubricating oil sales beginning July 1, 2026, lets the division set the fee from July 1, 2027, and allows grant funds to pay permitted transporters in curbside used oil collection.

ut:HB 370.title: Sex Offender Oversight Amendments
ut:HB 370.summary: Requires a monitoring program for sex offenders who cannot provide a residential address, creates penalties for noncompliance, and sets duties for local law enforcement and Adult Probation and Parole, including arrest warrant procedures.

ut:HB 376.title: Land Management Funding Amendments
ut:HB 376.summary: Establishes the Utah Forest Restoration Institute with Utah State University, funds it, and has it research forest and watershed health, coordinate restoration funding with the Watershed Restoration Initiative, and monitor project results.

ut:HB 378.title: Fugitive Dust Mitigation Amendments
ut:HB 378.summary: Lets the Division of Air Quality charge aggregate operations a compliance fee for fugitive dust, lets the Air Quality Board set the amount by rule from July 1, 2028, and requires public signage at fugitive dust facilities.

ut:HB 381.title: Electric Mobility Device Amendments
ut:HB 381.summary: Bans drinking alcohol while riding an electric-assisted bicycle, requires riders under 21 to wear helmets on certain electric devices on highways, lets officers hold a minor's electric vehicle for a parent, and creates a safety course.

ut:HB 382.title: Uniform Assignment for Benefit of Creditors Amendments
ut:HB 382.summary: Enacts the Uniform Assignment for Benefit of Creditors Act, setting rules for assignees, creditor claims, distribution priority and court oversight, and repeals the existing assignment for benefit of creditors code.

ut:HB 385.title: Specialized Product Sales Amendments
ut:HB 385.summary: Creates a Department of Agriculture license for specialized product retailers, requires ownership disclosure, limits e-cigarette advertising locations, and makes negligent sales of tobacco or nicotine to minors a crime.

ut:HB 389.title: Cannabis Amendments
ut:HB 389.summary: Requires industrial hemp retailers to check that buyers are 21, moves the medical cannabis program from the health department to the Department of Agriculture and Food, and lets medical cannabis pharmacies sell low-THC products.

ut:HB 401.title: Geothermal Study Amendments
ut:HB 401.summary: Directs Utah State University to study the geological and environmental impacts of geothermal energy development in the state and report to a legislative interim committee.

ut:HB 404.title: Sex-Designated Housing Amendments
ut:HB 404.summary: Lets landlords limit occupancy of single-sex housing to people of the designated biological sex and provides that doing so is not unlawful discrimination under the Utah Fair Housing Act.

ut:HB 408.title: Data Sharing Amendments
ut:HB 408.summary: Requires social media platforms to share user data in real time when users move to another platform, lets users choose which data to transfer, and requires consent before others' comments are included.

ut:HB 41.title: Construction and Fire Codes Amendments
ut:HB 41.summary: Updates the State Construction Code to current wildland-urban interface standards, delays the annual fee on high-risk wildland-urban interface property, and requires the division to share its wildfire risk mapping tool and respond to county-recommended changes.

ut:HB 410.title: Water Leasing Amendments
ut:HB 410.summary: Creates a Great Salt Lake Preservation Program and Board to lease water for the lake, sets the leasing process, and makes program appropriations nonlapsing.

ut:HB 412.title: Energy Development Planning Amendments
ut:HB 412.summary: Requires local governments to consult the Division of Wildlife Resources before approving utility-scale solar and wind power plants, sets the consultation requirements, and gives the division rulemaking authority.

ut:HB 416.title: First Responder Health Modifications
ut:HB 416.summary: Creates the Firefighter Cancer Benefit Trust Fund with a board of trustees and changes the amount of insurance premiums tax revenue transferred to the Utah State Retirement Office for certain firefighter retirement programs.

ut:HB 419.title: Environmental Legal Action Amendments
ut:HB 419.summary: Expands the definition of environmental action, which carries bond requirements, to include judicial review of certain permits issued by the Division of Oil, Gas, and Mining.

ut:HB 420.title: Municipal Office Vacancy Modifications
ut:HB 420.summary: Changes how vacancies in municipal offices are filled and how ties are broken in votes of a municipal legislative body.

ut:HB 423.title: Hit and Run and DUI Offense Amendments
ut:HB 423.summary: Increases penalties for leaving the scene of an accident for people previously convicted of that offense or DUI, creates mitigation for a negative chemical test, and changes DUI license hearing deadlines.

ut:HB 429.title: Special Districts Amendments
ut:HB 429.summary: Sets processes for a first-class county to withdraw from a first responder district and for a first-class county or municipality in it to withdraw from a garbage disposal district, including feasibility studies, hearings, and a freeze on the district's new debt.

ut:HB 436.title: Moderate Income Housing Infrastructure Amendments
ut:HB 436.summary: Changes what municipalities must report on moderate income housing for 2026 and gives the Transportation Commission priority consideration for certain projects where new residential units grow 2.5% or more.

ut:HB 437.title: Environmental Permitting Amendments
ut:HB 437.summary: Lets the Department of Environmental Quality and the Division of Oil, Gas, and Mining make rules for expedited review of eligible permits by certified qualified reviewers, with maximum review times, followed by a technical review and final decision.

ut:HB 447.title: Tobacco Amendments
ut:HB 447.summary: Allows remote retail sales of cigars and pipe tobacco by phone, mail or internet, with licensing, bonding and taxation of remote sellers and a criminal penalty for noncompliance.

ut:HB 454.title: Public Assistance Fraud Amendments
ut:HB 454.summary: Amends criminal provisions on obtaining public assistance, creates an offense of fraud by a person facilitating an inaccurate public assistance application, and adds it to the list of pattern of unlawful activity offenses.

ut:HB 457.title: County Governance Modifications
ut:HB 457.summary: Requires certain unincorporated islands in second-class counties to be annexed automatically by a bordering municipality unless local legislative bodies exempt them, with county notice required.

ut:HB 462.title: School Bus Internet Access
ut:HB 462.summary: Creates a grant program for rural school districts to install and operate internet connectivity on school buses, with priority criteria, long-term operation commitments and State Board of Education rules.

ut:HB 471.title: Social Services Amendments
ut:HB 471.summary: Changes Medicaid and SNAP rules, including work requirements, citizenship and verification standards, disenrollment after death or leaving the state, and limits on retroactive Medicaid eligibility, and adds reporting requirements.

ut:HB 473.title: Colorado River Authority Amendments
ut:HB 473.summary: Moves the Colorado River Authority of Utah from the governor's office to the Department of Natural Resources, changes its membership and appointment process, expands its powers, and repeals the Colorado River Authority Restricted Account.

ut:HB 474.title: Uniform Commercial Code Modifications
ut:HB 474.summary: Updates the Uniform Commercial Code, including replacing "writing" with "record," and adding rules on controllable electronic records, electronic documents of title, and security interests in related collateral.

ut:HB 475.title: Development Planning and Coordination Amendments
ut:HB 475.summary: Renames the Governor's Office of Economic Opportunity as the Governor's Office of Economic Development, changes the executive director's duties, and creates an Economic Development Council with reporting requirements.

ut:HB 48.title: Criminal and Juvenile Justice Changes
ut:HB 48.summary: Defines recidivism terms and changes the rules for provisionally housing a minor tried as an adult for aggravated murder in a secure care facility, including letting a prosecutor file a motion with the Board of Pardons and Parole.

ut:HB 481.title: Transportation Modifications
ut:HB 481.summary: Repeals the clean vehicle program, changes how standard and special group license plates are designed and issued, changes road usage charge rates, and allows flexible distribution timing for class B and C road funds.

ut:HB 492.title: Transportation, Infrastructure, and Housing Amendments
ut:HB 492.summary: Creates a State Housing Infrastructure Partnership Fund and board to lend to local governments for infrastructure that facilitates housing, and changes affordable housing infrastructure grant rules.

ut:HB 495.title: Capital Felony Case Amendments
ut:HB 495.summary: Changes procedures in death penalty cases, including appointing appellate counsel after a death sentence, rules for deciding intellectual disability, appeals of those rulings, stays of execution, and competency-to-be-executed petitions.

ut:HB 496.title: Forestry and Fire Amendments
ut:HB 496.summary: Gives the Division of Forestry, Fire, and State Lands enforcement and investigatory powers over wildland fires and heritage trees, and changes use of money from forest management cooperative agreements.

ut:HB 507.title: State Coordination of Regional and Local Economic Development Projects Amendments
ut:HB 507.summary: Bars local governments from giving incentives to large-load data centers with exceptions, creates a State Reinvestment Restricted Account and an optional county energy excise tax, and ends creation of certain reinvestment zones after January 1, 2028.

ut:HB 508.title: State Facilities Modifications
ut:HB 508.summary: Raises from $100,000 to $1.5 million the project cost for which a state entity may directly supervise facility construction, and changes capital project funding request steps, including for higher education.

ut:HB 509.title: Wetlands Study Amendments
ut:HB 509.summary: Directs the Department of Natural Resources to study wetlands in first- and second-class counties, report recommendations to a legislative committee, and restores its duty to publish wetlands land use permits.

ut:HB 51.title: Adoption Amendments
ut:HB 51.summary: Changes adoption rules for child-placing agencies, including licensing, advertising, reporting and disclosures, clarifies permissible payments and fees, and addresses birth parent consent revocation, therapy and transportation of birth mothers to Utah.

ut:HB 514.title: Utah Energy Council Amendments
ut:HB 514.summary: Creates the Utah Energy Infrastructure Service District, a state political subdivision that can own and operate energy facilities and issue revenue bonds, and expands the Utah Energy Council from five to seven members.

ut:HB 520.title: Higher Education Student Housing Study
ut:HB 520.summary: Requires a governor's office employee, with the commissioner of higher education, to study how higher education student housing affects surrounding communities and report to the Higher Education Appropriations Subcommittee.

ut:HB 536.title: Criminal Conduct on Public Lands Amendments
ut:HB 536.summary: Creates a Public Lands Restoration and Protection Fund, expands the graffiti offense on public lands to cover natural and archaeological features, changes antiquities-damage penalties, and lets courts direct restitution into the fund.

ut:HB 537.title: Olympic Ticket Sales Tax Exemption
ut:HB 537.summary: Exempts sales of tickets to the 2034 Olympic and Paralympic Winter Games from sales and use tax.

ut:HB 539.title: Public Safety Modifications
ut:HB 539.summary: Expands the definition of a domestic violence offense, changes bail, appearance and response rules, and bars certain jail release agreements from preventing contact with a minor child.

ut:HB 54.title: Boating Safety Education
ut:HB 54.summary: Requires motorboat and sailboat operators to complete a state safety course each calendar year and carry proof, with violations an infraction. Liveries may rent only to those with proof or after giving a safety briefing. Starts January 1, 2027.

ut:HB 540.title: Judicial Transparency and Information Access Amendments
ut:HB 540.summary: Requires the Judicial Council to create one website for all public court records, sets rules on access to audio recordings of public court proceedings and on records fees, and requires a rule on judicial financial disclosures.

ut:HB 545.title: Budgetary Modifications
ut:HB 545.summary: Renames some state funds, repeals several accounts and funds, and changes state grant rules, including barring administering agencies from using direct-award grant money for administration unless the appropriation allows it.

ut:HB 546.title: Public Lands Duty of Care Amendments
ut:HB 546.summary: Asserts the state's jurisdictional interest in federally controlled land and directs the Public Lands Policy Coordinating Office to map landscape-scale public lands, including forested "landscape public nuisance areas," and report annually.

ut:HB 557.title: Revisor's Technical Corrections to Utah Code
ut:HB 557.summary: Makes technical corrections to the Utah Code, such as fixing references to repealed provisions, removing obsolete language, updating cross-references, and repealing sunset and repeal dates that have passed.

ut:HB 565.title: City Library Property Tax Amendments
ut:HB 565.summary: Requires counties to list city library property tax levies separately on certain notices sent to property owners in a first-class county.

ut:HB 572.title: Behavioral Health, Mental Health, and Social Services Amendments
ut:HB 572.summary: Moves the Governor's Suicide Prevention Fund to the Office of Substance Use and Mental Health, creates a peer support specialist program, changes involuntary commitment and assisted outpatient treatment rules, adds a family outreach specialist after suicides or overdoses, and appropriates $750,000.

ut:HB 575.title: Fuel Tax and Supply Amendments
ut:HB 575.summary: Reduces the motor fuel tax rate, requires refineries to report production to the Office of Energy Development, and sets permitting and right-of-way coordination provisions for certain oil and gas pipelines.

ut:HB 591.title: Nuisance Amendments
ut:HB 591.summary: Rewrites Utah's nuisance laws, ends common-law public and private nuisance lawsuits except for the attorney general, and creates statutory rights of action and defenses for both.

ut:HB 599.title: Social Services Funding Amendments
ut:HB 599.summary: Moves the Children's Health Insurance Program into Medicaid, requires immunosuppressive drugs on the Medicaid preferred drug list, sends Medicaid ACA Fund interest to the General Fund, and directs e-cigarette proceeds to substance use treatment and prevention.

ut:HB 68.title: Housing and Community Development Amendments
ut:HB 68.summary: Creates a Division of Housing and Community Development in the Governor's Office of Economic Opportunity with a governor-appointed state housing coordinator, repeals the Commission on Housing Affordability, and moves the Homeless Housing and Services Grant Program.

ut:HB 69.title: Drinking Water Restructuring Amendments
ut:HB 69.summary: Lets a court appoint a receiver for a public water system supplier or order a violator to sell the system after Safe Drinking Water Act violations, and requires the director to report to a legislative committee when seeking such outcomes.

ut:HB 78.title: Nuclear Regulatory Amendments
ut:HB 78.summary: Creates a Nuclear Energy Regulatory Office within the Division of Waste Management and Radiation Control, authorizes licensing fees and new positions, and directs the division to seek expanded Agreement State status from the U.S. Nuclear Regulatory Commission.

ut:HB 8.title: State Agency Fees and Internal Service Fund Authorization and Appropriations
ut:HB 8.summary: Adjusts state agency and higher education budgets for fiscal years 2026 and 2027, authorizes certain state agency fees and internal service fund rates, and adjusts funding for internal service fund rate changes.

ut:HB 87.title: Animal Crime Victim Amendments
ut:HB 87.summary: Changes the rules for where officers may place animals seized in animal abuse cases, including a requirement that the recipient keep the former owner away from the animal.

ut:HB 89.title: Use of Polygraph Amendments
ut:HB 89.summary: Limits the use of a polygraph on a victim of a sexual offense.

ut:HCR 10.title: Concurrent Resolution Directing PEHP Regarding Hormone Replacement Therapy
ut:HCR 10.summary: Directs the Public Employees' Benefit and Insurance Program to provide hormone replacement therapy for menopausal symptoms.

ut:HCR 4.title: Concurrent Resolution Regarding Religious Freedom
ut:HCR 4.summary: Expresses support for public school students' and teachers' expression of faith, accommodation of religious observances, religious symbols in public spaces, and respectful dialogue among faiths.

ut:HCR 7.title: Concurrent Resolution Regarding Scenic Byway Designations
ut:HCR 7.summary: Approves the updated corridor management plan for the Zion Scenic Byway.

ut:HCR 8.title: Concurrent Resolution Directing PEHP to Establish the Weight Management and Obesity Pilot Program
ut:HCR 8.summary: Directs the Public Employees' Benefit Insurance Program to create a Weight Management and Obesity Pilot Program combining its bariatric surgery pilot with an option for GLP-1 coverage.

ut:HCR 9.title: Concurrent Resolution Addressing the Great Salt Lake
ut:HCR 9.summary: Urges the federal government to provide assistance to stabilize and restore the Great Salt Lake, and describes the lake's importance and Utah's restoration efforts.

ut:SB 101.title: Specialized Product Amendments
ut:SB 101.summary: Creates registration and licensing fees for cannabinoid and kratom products, applies a tax to kratom products, creates a temporary location sales license for specialized product retailers, and sets penalties.

ut:SB 110.title: Marriage Amendments
ut:SB 110.summary: Provides that a marriage that was not properly solemnized is valid only if someone files a petition for a court to recognize it before May 5, 2027.

ut:SB 121.title: Medical Cannabis Program Amendments
ut:SB 121.summary: Changes medical cannabis rules on labeling, transport, delivery storage, ID and card processes, allows guardian cards for incapacitated adults, creates a patient voucher program for cannabis or devices, and extends a governance working group's repeal date.

ut:SB 135.title: Nuclear Reprocessing Amendments
ut:SB 135.summary: Authorizes the Office of Energy Development to coordinate nuclear fuel recycling facility development and pursue a Nuclear Lifecycle Innovation Campus, and the Utah Energy Council to give guidance and assessments, with added annual reporting.

ut:SB 148.title: General Oversight Amendments
ut:SB 148.summary: Renames the Rules Review and General Oversight Committee as the General Oversight Committee, changes its membership, powers and closed-meeting rules, changes administrative rulemaking procedures, and repeals the governor's authority to revive rules the Legislature declined to reauthorize.

ut:SB 150.title: Healthcare Providers Scope of Practice Amendments
ut:SB 150.summary: Requires the Office of Professional Licensure Review to conduct scope-of-practice reviews of healthcare occupations on request and report recommendations to a legislative committee.

ut:SB 151.title: Public Safety Funding Amendments
ut:SB 151.summary: Changes permitted uses of the Transportation Investment Fund of 2005 to include operating state highways, including traffic enforcement, if built or renovated with fund money, and addresses funding for the Motor Vehicle Safety Impact Restricted Account.

ut:SB 174.title: Exercise of Religious Beliefs and Conscience Amendments
ut:SB 174.summary: Allows health care providers to refuse to provide or take part in services that violate their religious or conscience beliefs, bars liability and retaliation, requires advance notice to the institution, and allows legal action for violations.

ut:SB 184.title: Justice System Amendments
ut:SB 184.summary: Lets city attorneys employ or temporarily deputize attorneys as prosecutors, and lets a court enter a conviction for a lower degree of offense if a defendant substantially assists another case within a year of sentencing.

ut:SB 195.title: Workforce Development
ut:SB 195.summary: Creates a Statewide Youth Apprenticeship Governance Council, lets the governor delegate approval of eligible workforce programs to the Utah Board of Higher Education, and authorizes participation in the federal Workforce Pell Grant program.

ut:SB 197.title: Transportation Funding and Governance Amendments
ut:SB 197.summary: Replaces the large public transit district board with a transit commission, has the governor appoint the executive director, and directs a share of new state sales tax growth to the Transit Transportation Investment Fund starting in fiscal 2028.

ut:SB 2.title: Public Education Budget Amendments
ut:SB 2.summary: Adjusts public education appropriations for fiscal year 2026 and sets them for fiscal year 2027, repeals the Digital Teaching and Learning Grant Program, and changes rules on educator salary adjustments and Private Course Choice scholarship funds.

ut:SB 20.title: Natural Resources, Agriculture, and Environment Technical Changes
ut:SB 20.summary: Repeals outdated programs, reports, studies and deadlines in natural resources, agriculture and environment law, requires certain annual reports by October 1, and makes technical corrections.

ut:SB 201.title: Shelter Animal Euthanasia Amendments
ut:SB 201.summary: Allows animal shelters to euthanize dogs and cats only if no reasonable alternatives to euthanasia are available.

ut:SB 209.title: Gooseberry Narrows State Park Study
ut:SB 209.summary: Requires the Division of State Parks to study the feasibility and cost of building a state park and dam in the Gooseberry Narrows and to report the results to a legislative interim committee.

ut:SB 21.title: Geothermal Amendments
ut:SB 21.summary: Changes geothermal resource law, including reservation of geothermal resources on state trust land, ownership of geothermal resources or fluids, confidentiality of information, and bonding requirements.

ut:SB 229.title: State Employee Benefits Amendments
ut:SB 229.summary: Creates a paid time off program replacing annual and sick leave for new and electing state employees, converts accrued annual leave one-to-one, changes the 401(k) match, and requires agency leave banks.

ut:SB 234.title: Rulemaking Amendments
ut:SB 234.summary: Bars certain state environmental health and waste management rules from being more stringent or broader than federal law and requires agencies to support certain such rules with scientific evidence.

ut:SB 242.title: Transportation Amendments
ut:SB 242.summary: Makes transportation changes, including a road usage charge on commercial electric vehicles of 6,001 pounds or more, a sales tax exemption on transit construction materials, and increased commuter rail bonding authority.

ut:SB 251.title: Local Health Department and Department of Environmental Quality Coordination
ut:SB 251.summary: Lets local governments and health departments request state reimbursement for extraordinary costs of environmental enforcement activities, and removes a department reporting requirement to a legislative committee.

ut:SB 252.title: Water Usage at State-owned Facilities Amendments
ut:SB 252.summary: Requires state agencies to take steps on irrigation and low-water turf at state facilities, and directs the Division of Facilities Construction and Management to audit irrigation systems.

ut:SB 254.title: Extracted Natural Resources Amendments
ut:SB 254.summary: Speeds environmental and mining permitting, creates a Critical Minerals Council and process to designate critical minerals zones, and creates a State Reinvestment Restricted Account fed by severance tax revenue.

ut:SB 26.title: Pest Control Amendments
ut:SB 26.summary: Changes pest control regulation by modifying pesticide applicator business fees and registration, repealing the qualified party concept, and creating permits, with fines, for ornamental and turf technicians and certain salespersons.

ut:SB 270.title: State Court Amendments
ut:SB 270.summary: Lets the Judicial Council create a division within the district court, addresses its resources and case transfers, and changes how many applicants the nominating commission sends the governor when several appellate vacancies exist.

ut:SB 287.title: Targeted Advertising Tax
ut:SB 287.summary: Imposes an annual tax on entities above revenue thresholds, based on their gross receipts from targeted advertising delivered in Utah, with revenue deposited in a restricted account.

ut:SB 295.title: Intellectual Diversity in Education and Government
ut:SB 295.summary: Changes rules on discriminatory practices, training and clubs in public schools, colleges and state government, and requires universities to hold public policy events, such as debates, with differing perspectives.

ut:SB 3.title: Current Fiscal Year Supplemental Appropriations
ut:SB 3.summary: Adjusts appropriations for state government for the fiscal year ending June 30, 2026, including higher education and state agencies, authorizes full-time employment levels for internal service funds, and includes intent language.

ut:SB 312.title: Educator License Amendments
ut:SB 312.summary: Sets tiered restrictions on school employment and volunteering after educator license suspension or revocation: automatic for serious misconduct harming or risking children, written findings required otherwise, and technical violations exempt.

ut:SB 45.title: Kratom Adjustments
ut:SB 45.summary: Requires kratom processors and retailers to register with the Department of Agriculture and Food, limits kratom sales to retail tobacco specialty businesses, bans some kratom products, changes the purchase age, and classifies high-concentration 7-hydroxymitragynine as a Schedule I drug.

ut:SB 46.title: Water Wise Landscaping Amendments
ut:SB 46.summary: Imposes water wise landscaping requirements on state government facilities.

ut:SB 66.title: Medical Cannabis Pharmacy License Amendments
ut:SB 66.summary: Clarifies and changes the authority of the Department of Agriculture and Food to set geographic regions for medical cannabis pharmacy locations.

ut:SB 8.title: State Agency and Higher Education Compensation Appropriations
ut:SB 8.summary: Funds a 2.5% labor market pay increase for state and higher education employees, health and dental cost changes, retirement rate changes, and a state match of up to $26 per pay period for employees in a defined contribution plan.

ut:SB 98.title: Substance Use Rehabilitation Amendments
ut:SB 98.summary: Allows the Department of Health and Human Services to create a certification program for employers as recovery ready workplaces, with an application process and criteria, and allows e-cigarette proceeds funding for it.

ut:SCR 10.title: Concurrent Resolution Emphasizing Utah's Commitment to Advanced Air Mobility
ut:SCR 10.summary: Recognizes Utah's aerospace history and sets a long-term goal of an operating Advanced Air Mobility system and vertiport network before the 2034 Winter Olympics, with federal collaboration.

ut:SCR 6.title: Concurrent Resolution Regarding Pediatric Care for Autonomic Disorders
ut:SCR 6.summary: Encourages the medical community to raise awareness, education and diagnosis of POTS and related autonomic disorders in children, and encourages insurers to cover diagnosis and treatment.

ut:SCR 7.title: Concurrent Resolution on State Innovation for Transition from Government Benefits to Self-reliance
ut:SCR 7.summary: Urges the federal government to give states more flexibility to run experiments and pilots helping families move off government benefits and into work, citing the "benefits cliff" and "benefits plateau."

ut:SCR 9.title: Concurrent Resolution Regarding Critical Minerals Development and Funding
ut:SCR 9.summary: Expresses support for creating a state MINES Center for critical minerals, urges the federal government to distribute critical minerals money through block grants, and calls on Utah's congressional delegation to back a national lab designation and funding.

wa:HB 1128.title: Establishing a child care workforce standards board.
wa:HB 1128.summary: Creates a 10-member Child Care Workforce Standards Board, appointed by the Governor and supported by Labor and Industries, to recommend improvements to employment standards for child care workers, considering staffing, wages and ratios.

wa:HB 1170.title: Informing users when content is developed or modified by artificial intelligence.
wa:HB 1170.summary: Requires publicly accessible generative AI providers with over 1 million monthly users to include hard-to-remove provenance data in AI-made or altered video, image and audio content, and requires government consumer-facing AI systems to disclose they are AI.

wa:HB 1187.title: Protecting patients involved in motor vehicle accidents from delayed ambulance bills.
wa:HB 1187.summary: Bars ambulance services from selling or assigning medical debt from a motor vehicle accident to a collection agency until 120 days after the first bill is sent. Lets the Insurance Commissioner refer patterns of billing violations to the Department of Health.

wa:HB 1295.title: Using evidence-based instructional practices in reading and writing literacy for public elementary students.
wa:HB 1295.summary: Starting September 1, 2027, requires school districts and charter schools updating or buying K-4 reading and writing curriculum to choose curriculum with specified components, including phonological awareness, fluency and vocabulary, aligned to state standards.

wa:HB 1390.title: Repealing the community protection program.
wa:HB 1390.summary: Removes the Community Protection Program from state law effective January 1, 2027, and directs the Department of Social and Health Services to move all participants into other services or programs by December 31, 2026.

wa:HB 1500.title: Concerning resale certificates for units in common interest communities.
wa:HB 1500.summary: Requires condominium and homeowners' association resale certificates to include the latest financial audit, board-approved policies, and the full current reserve study, and marks any missing category "NONE" or "RECORDS UNAVAILABLE".

wa:HB 1501.title: Concerning inquiries into association governance or operations by unit owners in common interest communities.
wa:HB 1501.summary: Lets condominium and homeowners' association members send written inquiries about governance by certified mail, and requires the association to respond within 30 days, with extensions allowed. Legal-opinion costs count as a common expense.

wa:HB 1526.title: Modifying the snack bar liquor license.
wa:HB 1526.summary: Allows retailers holding a snack bar liquor license, which covers on-site beer sales, to also sell wine by the glass for on-premises consumption.

wa:HB 1701.title: Authorizing multiple liquor licensees to have licensed premises within a facility owned and leased out by another liquor licensee or person.
wa:HB 1701.summary: Allows multiple liquor licensees to operate separate premises at one facility, which one of them may own and lease to others. Lets a licensee lease its kitchen to another person, with no profit or revenue sharing.

wa:HB 1710.title: Concerning compliance with the Washington voting rights act of 2018.
wa:HB 1710.summary: Adds preclearance to the Washington Voting Rights Act: local governments with qualifying histories of voting-rights violations must obtain a certificate of no objection from the Attorney General before changing election methods, boundaries or similar voting policies.

wa:HB 1750.title: Creating guidelines for voter suppression and vote dilution claims under the Washington voting rights act.
wa:HB 1750.summary: Changes the Washington Voting Rights Act so local governments violate it if an election policy or practice creates a material disparate burden on protected-class voters' ability to vote, unless narrowly tailored to a compelling interest with no less-burdensome alternative.

wa:HB 1796.title: Concerning school districts' authority to contract indebtedness for school construction.
wa:HB 1796.summary: Lets school districts borrow and issue bonds for buildings, furniture and equipment without a public vote, within a 0.375 percent debt limit. Districts must delay receiving state school construction assistance for those projects.

wa:HB 1903.title: Establishing a statewide low-income energy assistance program.
wa:HB 1903.summary: Creates a statewide low-income energy assistance program in the Department of Commerce that, subject to appropriation, gives funds to participating utilities to reduce low-income customers' monthly energy bills, phased in under rules.

wa:HB 1906.title: Increasing transparency and consumer protection in water system rates.
wa:HB 1906.summary: Requires public water systems to notify counties and neighboring systems before ownership changes, and requires the Utilities and Transportation Commission to adopt rate rules accounting for outside funding, approved water system plans, and notice of capital projects.

wa:HB 1909.title: Establishing the court unification task force.
wa:HB 1909.summary: Creates a Court Unification Task Force of legislators, judges, court clerks, local officials and legal professionals to analyze the state court system and identify where more centralized operations could improve efficiency, uniformity and access.

wa:HB 1916.title: Amending voter registration challenges and managing voter registration lists.
wa:HB 1916.summary: Limits who may challenge a voter's registration to registered voters in the same county, and removes requirements that challengers show they searched property, phone, and other-state registration records when claiming the voter does not live at the address.

wa:HB 1941.title: Authorizing agricultural cooperatives for cannabis producers.
wa:HB 1941.summary: Lets licensed cannabis producers form agricultural associations or cooperatives to collectively process, handle or market their products. Each association may represent no more than three producer licenses.

wa:HB 1960.title: Encouraging renewable energy in Washington through tax policy and investment in local communities.
wa:HB 1960.summary: Exempts from property tax personal property of wind and solar facilities of at least 10 MW starting 2028, and of battery storage systems starting 2029. Excludes the added value from levy calculations.

wa:HB 1974.title: Establishing land banking authorities.
wa:HB 1974.summary: Lets cities and counties authorize a public corporation, housing authority or nonprofit to operate a land bank that acquires, holds and sells or leases property, with transfers at below-market rates to developers who meet affordable housing requirements.

wa:HB 2034.title: Concerning termination and restatement of plan 1 of the law enforcement officers' and firefighters' retirement system.
wa:HB 2034.summary: Terminates the LEOFF Plan 1 pension system on June 30, 2029, and creates a restated system paying the same benefits. Assets above 110 percent of liabilities move to a state holding account that the Legislature may transfer to the general fund.

wa:HB 2091.title: Requiring public employers under chapter 41.80 RCW to provide employee information to exclusive bargaining representatives.
wa:HB 2091.summary: Extends the requirement that public employers give exclusive bargaining representatives employee information to all employers covered by the Personnel System Reform Act, with no liability if their current technology cannot supply it.

wa:HB 2156.title: Concerning the authority of investigators of the attorney general's office.
wa:HB 2156.summary: Requires the Attorney General to designate investigators for economic and financial crimes as limited-authority peace officers with CJTC training. They cannot be armed, arrest or detain, or physically serve warrants, and warrants served electronically need judicial approval.

wa:HB 2165.title: Concerning false identification as a peace officer.
wa:HB 2165.summary: Makes it a gross misdemeanor to claim to be a peace officer, or to use a vehicle, clothing or insignia to give that impression, when a reasonable person would believe the person is a peace officer.

wa:HB 2192.title: Updating the role of the Washington traffic safety commission in identifying the risk factors that lead to roadway fatalities.
wa:HB 2192.summary: Designates the Washington Traffic Safety Commission a public health authority, letting it receive crash, toxicology and fatality driver-license records, and review pedestrian and bicyclist deaths with its council.

wa:HB 2219.title: Enhancing the operational efficiency of child care providers.
wa:HB 2219.summary: Requires child care licensing to suspend a license immediately if high-potency synthetic opioids or drug-making equipment are found on site, allows up to 2.5 hours a day of mixed-age ratio time in centers, and waives repeat orientation in some cases.

wa:HB 2225.title: Concerning regulation of artificial intelligence companion chatbots.
wa:HB 2225.summary: Requires operators of AI companion chatbots to disclose the bot is not human, with repeat notices every three hours (hourly for known minors), and to take measures against sexually explicit content and manipulative engagement with minors.

wa:HB 2251.title: Concerning climate commitment act accounts.
wa:HB 2251.summary: Repeals several Climate Commitment Act accounts and replaces them with an operating account and a capital account, renames the carbon emissions reduction account as a transportation account, and caps Ecology administrative costs at $25 million a year.

wa:HB 2266.title: Encouraging permanent supportive housing, transitional housing, indoor emergency housing, and indoor emergency shelters.
wa:HB 2266.summary: Requires cities and counties to allow transitional and permanent supportive housing wherever housing or hotels are allowed inside urban growth areas, and indoor emergency shelters wherever hotels are allowed. These uses may not be placed in industrial zones.

wa:HB 2274.title: Modifying the Washington commercial electronic mail act.
wa:HB 2274.summary: Under the commercial email law, requires proof that the sender knew a subject line was false or misleading, and lowers statutory damages for prohibited commercial emails or texts to $100 or actual damages, whichever is greater.

wa:HB 2320.title: Concerning the regulation of firearm manufacturing.
wa:HB 2320.summary: Bars making untraceable firearms, frames or receivers with 3D printers, CNC milling machines or other means, with exceptions, and bars selling or distributing digital firearm manufacturing code to people not federally licensed to manufacture. Penalties range from civil infractions to felonies.

wa:HB 2325.title: Establishing a tourism self-supported assessment program to fund statewide tourism promotion.
wa:HB 2325.summary: Creates a Tourism Assessment Program in which the Washington Tourism Marketing Authority levies an annual assessment, set as a percentage of gross revenue, on tourism-related businesses after industry sector ratification. A Ratepayer Oversight Board designs the program and proposes budgets.

wa:HB 2334.title: Adjusting the price of a cash transaction to eliminate the need for pennies.
wa:HB 2334.summary: Allows businesses to round in-person cash transaction totals to the nearest five cents, with 1-2 cent endings rounded down and 3-4 cent endings rounded up. Card payments are not rounded, and customers with exact change may pay the unrounded price.

wa:HB 2384.title: Increasing regulatory oversight of continuing care retirement communities.
wa:HB 2384.summary: Requires continuing care retirement communities offering life care contracts to submit an actuarial analysis to the Department of Social and Health Services, beginning July 1, 2027, with every other registration renewal after the second.

wa:HB 2410.title: Establishing a commercial truck safety and education council.
wa:HB 2410.summary: Establishes a Commercial Truck Safety and Education Council within the Washington Traffic Safety Commission to recommend programs and projects that improve safety in the commercial trucking industry.

wa:HB 2416.title: Concerning fair treatment of waste to energy facilities under the climate commitment act.
wa:HB 2416.summary: Requires Ecology to give a pre-1992 waste-to-energy facility that becomes a covered entity no-cost carbon allowances through 2030: 100 percent of baseline emissions in 2027–28, falling to 86 percent in 2030, with 40 percent consigned to auction.

wa:HB 2442.title: Providing local governments tax resources and fund flexibility.
wa:HB 2442.summary: Authorizes counties and cities to impose a new sales tax of up to 0.01 percent for children and family services starting 2027, and widens allowed uses of real estate excise, housing sales tax and other local revenues.

wa:HB 2445.title: Ending probates for profit.
wa:HB 2445.summary: Extends waiting periods before courts appoint a public guardian or "suitable person" to administer an estate, limits "suitable person" appointments to two a year, and disqualifies people with recent fiduciary misconduct findings or ties to buyers of estate property.

wa:HB 2487.title: Concerning taxes imposed on insurers operating within the state.
wa:HB 2487.summary: Changes the insurance premium exemption from the business and occupation tax so it applies to insurers that pay Washington premium taxes, premiums of premium-tax-exempt persons, regulated annuities, and assigned risk plans. Applies retroactively.

wa:HB 2495.title: Addressing the removal of vehicles by certain cities when obstructing the operation of streetcar vehicles or jeopardizing public safety.
wa:HB 2495.summary: Allows cities over 700,000 residents to have vehicles that obstruct streetcar operations or jeopardize safety on streetcar rights-of-way immediately removed and impounded.

wa:HB 2496.title: Concerning tribal consultation conducted by the energy facility site evaluation council.
wa:HB 2496.summary: Requires the Energy Facility Site Evaluation Council to offer government-to-government consultation to the affected tribe within 90 days of a site certification application, and to meet with all members if the tribe asks.

wa:HB 2521.title: Concerning firearms background check.
wa:HB 2521.summary: Removes the $18 cap on the firearms background check fee and requires the State Patrol to set the fee at the amount needed to cover the program's total costs.

wa:HB 2539.title: Concerning inmate funds.
wa:HB 2539.summary: Raises the dollar threshold for classifying a prison inmate as indigent to $100, adjusts it for inflation every four years from July 2029, and requires the Department of Corrections to post the rate publicly each year.

wa:HB 2548.title: Strengthening health care market standards.
wa:HB 2548.summary: Expands the Attorney General's 60-day notice requirement to ownership changes, asset sales and nonprofit-to-for-profit conversions of hospitals and provider organizations. Adds filing fees and a 30-day wait after parties certify compliance with an information request.

wa:HB 2588.title: Concerning county ferry district authority.
wa:HB 2588.summary: Requires a county ferry district to cover the entire county and requires the county to appoint a five-member advisory committee of county residents, mostly frequent ferry users, serving four-year terms.

wa:HB 2594.title: Ensuring that unhoused children and youths in Washington have equal access to free, appropriate public education.
wa:HB 2594.summary: Sets state requirements, paralleling the federal McKinney-Vento Act, for the education of homeless children and youths, including a state coordinator, school district duties, and equal access to public education. Federal-compliant actions satisfy the state requirements.

wa:HB 2610.title: Ensuring nonprofit housing providers qualify for a property tax exemption when the property is temporarily used for certain community purposes other than affordable housing.
wa:HB 2610.summary: Lets nonprofits with the homeownership property tax exemption temporarily rent or lend the property to another organization without losing the exemption, requires an annual renewal declaration, and preserves the exemption on transfer to another exempt nonprofit.

wa:HB 2624.title: Clarifying consumer protections regarding unsolicited real estate transactions for public purposes or by nonprofit land conservancies.
wa:HB 2624.summary: Exempts public entities, tribes and nonprofit nature conservancies acquiring land for a public benefit, with an appraisal before closing, from the requirements for solicited real estate transactions, such as owner appraisal and cancellation rights.

wa:HB 2681.title: Modifying cannabis producer, processor, and retailer license fees. (REVISED FOR ENGROSSED: Concerning cannabis license fees.)
wa:HB 2681.summary: Raises annual cannabis producer, processor and retailer license fees from $1,381 to $1,781.

wa:HB 2689.title: Concerning the working connections child care program.
wa:HB 2689.summary: Keeps Working Connections Child Care income eligibility at 60 percent of state median income instead of raising it later, and sets subsidy base rates at the 75th percentile of market from July 2027.

wa:HB 2711.title: Concerning transportation resources.
wa:HB 2711.summary: Raises the aircraft fuel tax from 18 to 25 cents per gallon and doubles the aircraft registration fee to $30, raises aircraft excise taxes, repeals a planned luxury aircraft tax, and changes luxury vehicle and recreational vessel tax rules, including trade-in treatment.

wa:SB 5068.title: Concerning agencies, firefighters, prosecutors, and general or limited authority law enforcement, extending eligibility for employment to all United States citizens or persons legally authorized to work in the United States under federal law.
wa:SB 5068.summary: Lets law enforcement agencies hire jail and prison corrections officers, and prosecutors hire deputy prosecuting attorneys, who are legally authorized to work in the U.S. even if not citizens. Weapons bans based solely on immigration status do not bar certification.

wa:SB 5156.title: Concerning elevator standards in smaller apartment buildings.
wa:SB 5156.summary: Directs the State Building Code Council to set standards allowing minimally sized passenger elevators in apartment buildings of up to six stories and 24 units, and to convene a group to review hoistway protection and emergency communication rules.

wa:SB 5185.title: Establishing preceptorship and hardship pathways to medical practice for international medical graduates.
wa:SB 5185.summary: Creates a Washington Medical Commission pilot program giving internationally trained physicians a path to a primary care medical license through supervised clinical experience, and removes an existing licensure exemption for certain exceptional-ability immigrants.

wa:SB 5272.title: Improving school safety by extending penalties for interference by, or intimidation by threat of, force or violence at schools and extracurricular activities and requiring schools to notify the public of such penalties.
wa:SB 5272.summary: Extends the crimes of interference and intimidation by threat to school employees, contractors, students and athletic officials performing their duties, and allows excluding convicted people from the school and students from the activity.

wa:SB 5346.title: Restricting mobile device usage by public school students.
wa:SB 5346.summary: Adds mobile devices to digital citizenship instruction, authorizes school boards to adopt policies limiting student possession and use of mobile devices, and requires the state superintendent to report on school phone policies by December 15, 2027.

wa:SB 5520.title: Concerning the wrongly convicted persons act.
wa:SB 5520.summary: Revises the wrongly convicted persons compensation law, defining actual innocence by a preponderance of the evidence and adding "significant new exculpatory information," and sets conditions for filing a claim for state compensation.

wa:SB 5720.title: Enacting the uniform consumer debt default judgments act.
wa:SB 5720.summary: Sets requirements for default judgments in consumer debt collection cases, including required complaint details, debt documentation, chain-of-ownership information for purchased debt, and a notice to the consumer before a default judgment.

wa:SB 5820.title: Concerning the responsibility of certain counties to include freight rail dependent use overlay as part of the transportation element of their comprehensive plan.
wa:SB 5820.summary: Removes provisions letting western Washington counties with at least 400,000 residents bordering another state, and their cities, regulate rural and resource lands next to short line railroads for freight rail dependent uses.

wa:SB 5837.title: Concerning guardianship, conservatorship, and other protective arrangements.
wa:SB 5837.summary: Revises adult guardianship procedures, requiring a court-appointed attorney for the respondent when they object, request one, or their interests cannot otherwise be protected, and allowing first-class mail for court visitor statements.

wa:SB 5841.title: Concerning the completion of postsecondary financial aid applications.
wa:SB 5841.summary: Requires the high school and beyond plan platform to import financial aid application status data and send College Bound Scholarship students eligibility notices, and to record whether students completed financial aid applications.

wa:SB 5855.title: Concerning the use of face coverings by law enforcement officers.
wa:SB 5855.summary: Bars state, local and federal law enforcement officers from wearing opaque face coverings while interacting with the public on duty, except for undercover work, SWAT protective gear, or required safety equipment.

wa:SB 5892.title: Concerning protection of the voter registration database.
wa:SB 5892.summary: Bars county election offices from releasing voter registration database records and directs requesters to the Secretary of State, makes knowing violations or improper disclosures by election officers a class C felony, and limits sensitive voter data in public records.

wa:SB 5922.title: Authorizing transportation vehicle fund transfers.
wa:SB 5922.summary: Lets a school district that reduces its bus fleet petition the state superintendent to transfer money, including depreciation payments and interest, from its transportation vehicle fund to another fund; the petition must be approved if the reduction is appropriate.

wa:SB 5925.title: Concerning the general powers and duties of the attorney general’s office.
wa:SB 5925.summary: Lets the Attorney General issue civil investigative demands for documents, testimony and written answers when facts suggest possible violations of constitutional law, the law enforcement Keep Washington Working Act, wage laws, the Law Against Discrimination or the jails act, after attorney approval.

wa:SB 5937.title: Concerning the use of a smart access system in a residential property subject to the residential landlord-tenant act.
wa:SB 5937.summary: Requires landlords with smart access systems to offer tenants an alternative key not using biometrics or a phone app on request, and to provide a privacy policy listing the data collected and how it is used.

wa:SB 5938.title: Concerning the foreclosure prevention fee.
wa:SB 5938.summary: Changes the mortgage foreclosure prevention fee: exempts reverse mortgages for borrowers 60 and older and chattel dwelling loans, limits the fee to purchases of up to four units financed through state housing programs, and lets Commerce administer it.

wa:SB 5944.title: Concerning language access providers' collective bargaining.
wa:SB 5944.summary: Adds payment for appointments missed or canceled by others to what language access providers bargain over, and provides that a collective bargaining agreement prevails over conflicting executive orders, rules and policies, but is invalid where it conflicts with statute.

wa:SB 5974.title: Modernizing and strengthening laws concerning sheriffs, police chiefs, town marshals, law enforcement agency volunteers, youth cadets, specially commissioned officers, and police matrons.
wa:SB 5974.summary: Strike-and-replace amendment that sets eligibility for sheriffs, police chiefs and town marshals (age 25, five years' law enforcement experience, no felony, certification, background check), creates a vacancy on decertification, and limits roles of law enforcement volunteers.

wa:SB 5975.title: Providing consumer access to safe cookware and interstate and international trade certainty in the regulation of lead in cookware.
wa:SB 5975.summary: Bans selling aluminum or brass cookware with intentionally added lead from January 1, 2027, keeps a 90 ppm lead limit, and sets 50 ppm for aluminum or brass pots and pans from 2030 and 20 ppm from 2034.

wa:SB 5981.title: Protecting patient access to discounted medications and health care services through Washington's health care safety net by preventing manufacturer limitations on the 340B drug pricing program.
wa:SB 5981.summary: Bars drug manufacturers from restricting the purchase or delivery of 340B discounted drugs to covered health entities and their contract pharmacies, or from requiring claims data as a condition, unless federal law requires it. Lets covered entities sue.

wa:SB 5982.title: Updating provisions for consumer-owned utilities, including port districts, and affected market customers under the clean energy transformation act.
wa:SB 5982.summary: Adds port districts that distribute electricity to the definition of consumer-owned utility under the Clean Energy Transformation Act, and redefines "market customer" and its retail electric load for reporting and compliance.

wa:SB 5995.title: Concerning moneys available to a port district allocated for the purchase of zero and near zero emission cargo handling equipment.
wa:SB 5995.summary: Removes the December 31, 2031 expiration date from the port district law on cargo handling equipment funds, and bars port districts from using port funds to buy fully automated marine container cargo handling equipment after that date.

wa:SB 5998.title: Making 2025-2027 fiscal biennium supplemental operating appropriations.
wa:SB 5998.summary: Sets 2026 supplemental changes to the 2025–27 state operating budget, modifying appropriations for various state agencies and programs.

wa:SB 6005.title: Making supplemental transportation appropriations for the 2025-2027 fiscal biennium.
wa:SB 6005.summary: Sets 2026 supplemental changes to the 2025–27 state transportation budget, modifying appropriations for various state transportation agencies and programs.

wa:SB 6026.title: Concerning residential development in commercial and mixed-use zones.
wa:SB 6026.summary: Bars cities of 30,000 or more and non-rural counties planning under the Growth Management Act from excluding residential uses in commercial and mixed-use zones, with exceptions such as industrial zones, areas near refineries, and historic landmarks.

wa:SB 6027.title: Modifying requirements and allowed uses for certain funding related to providing and maintaining affordable housing and related services.
wa:SB 6027.summary: Expands allowed uses of the local housing sales tax, at least 60 percent for operating and rehabilitating existing affordable housing, and lets local governments pool tax receipts through interlocal agreements and pledge them to bonds.

wa:SB 6035.title: Ensuring access to voting services for military, overseas, Native American, and disabled voters.
wa:SB 6035.summary: Requires county auditors to meet with each federally recognized tribe by August 1 of odd-numbered years about voting centers and ballot drop boxes, and allows the Secretary of State to study an electronic ballot portal for service, overseas, disabled and reservation voters.

wa:SB 6066.title: Establishing accident risk zones.
wa:SB 6066.summary: Lets counties, cities and towns create crash prevention zones on roads with higher-than-expected serious-injury or fatal collisions: until 2029 only on three named highway segments, then generally, as can the state transportation department.

wa:SB 6076.title: Streamlining consumer-owned utility procurement requirements for clean energy generation, energy storage, transmission, and distribution projects.
wa:SB 6076.summary: Through 2044, raises public utility district procurement limits for renewable and non-emitting generation, storage and grid projects: no-contract work up to $500,000 and work by own staff up to $1 million, and allows electronic bids.

wa:SB 6081.title: Protecting Washingtonians from invasion of privacy, including the unauthorized disclosure of sex designation information and historic sex designation changes in official government records.
wa:SB 6081.summary: Exempts sex designation, and driver's license and permit change information, from public records disclosure, and bars the Department of Licensing from sharing sex designation change records with other jurisdictions without the person's consent.

wa:SB 6106.title: Modifying the securing timely notification and benefits for laid-off employees act. (REVISED FOR ENGROSSED: Concerning the laid-off employees act.)
wa:SB 6106.summary: Excludes Indian tribes from the layoff notice law's definition of employer, exempts employee names and addresses given to the Employment Security Department from public records, and limits where they must appear in layoff notices.

wa:SB 6113.title: Concerning taxes administered by the department of revenue.
wa:SB 6113.summary: Makes technical changes to recently enacted retail sales tax on services, including clarifying definitions for IT, staffing and live presentation services, applying use tax to the new services, and giving a transition period for existing contracts.

wa:SB 6137.title: Concerning the regulated sports wagering industry.
wa:SB 6137.summary: Allows sports wagering on college events involving Washington schools, but not on individual athletes enrolled at those schools, in-game coaching decisions, or officiating decisions.

wa:SB 6151.title: Concerning dedicated accounts for fees collected for the implementation of environmental programs.
wa:SB 6151.summary: Creates a Laboratory Accreditation Account to receive Ecology's lab accreditation fees, spendable after appropriation and fee rulemaking, to cover costs and clear the backlog of drinking water lab accreditations.

wa:SB 6162.title: Concerning property tax reform.
wa:SB 6162.summary: Exempts qualifying retired and disabled homeowners from the entire state property tax, raises income thresholds, and merges the two state levies into one state school levy set at $2.075355 per $1,000 for 2026.

wa:SB 6182.title: Establishing an abortion savings program.
wa:SB 6182.summary: Creates an Abortion Savings Program in which the Department of Health, subject to appropriation, gives operating grants to eligible abortion providers, funds and other organizations, funded by an assessment on health carriers per coverage month starting in 2027.

wa:SB 6188.title: Concerning the department of labor and industries' authority to enact rules related to regulating asbestos training.
wa:SB 6188.summary: Removes the limit on Labor and Industries asbestos certification rulemaking to federal-minimum rules, and instead requires rules based on best available evidence and industry standards that are the least burdensome necessary to address hazards.

wa:SB 6189.title: Changing the deadline for forming a public facilities district for regional aquatics and sports facilities.
wa:SB 6189.summary: Removes the deadline for contiguous cities, towns and counties that helped create a public facilities district to form an additional district for regional aquatics and sports facilities.

wa:SB 6200.title: Concerning renters' and mobile home occupants' ability to install portable cooling devices.
wa:SB 6200.summary: Bars landlords from prohibiting tenants from installing portable air conditioners or heat pumps, with exceptions for existing heat pumps, code, safety or electrical limits, and for window units that block egress or cannot be secured.

wa:SB 6225.title: Authorizing bonds for transportation funding.
wa:SB 6225.summary: Authorizes up to $800 million in state bonds for highway projects, deposited in the Move Ahead Washington Account, raises the State Route 520 bond authorization by $500 million to $2.45 billion, and expires certain unused bond authority.

wa:SB 6226.title: Protecting the clinical autonomy of audiologists.
wa:SB 6226.summary: Lets licensed professionals use clinical judgment to choose telehealth or in-person care when fitting and dispensing hearing instruments, without limiting the board's authority to set standards of care, supervision, documentation and safety rules.

wa:SB 6228.title: Removing a tax exemption for the warehousing and reselling of prescription drugs. (REVISED FOR ENGROSSED: Removing a tax exemption for the warehousing and reselling of prescription drugs and providing tax relief for critical access pharmacies.)
wa:SB 6228.summary: Repeals the 0.138 percent business tax rate for prescription drug wholesalers, setting 0.5 percent for 2027 and 0.35 percent from 2028, and creates a 0.138 percent rate for qualifying independent critical access pharmacies from 2027.

wa:SB 6231.title: Removing a tax exemption for the replacement of equipment for data centers.
wa:SB 6231.summary: Removes replacement servers from the data center sales and use tax exemption, ends new refurbishment certificates in rural counties from July 1, 2026 and expires existing ones that day, and ends the exemption for data centers refurbished after that date in counties over 800,000 residents.

wa:SB 6237.title: Concerning rental property disclosures of flooding history and flood risk.
wa:SB 6237.summary: Requires landlords, for leases entered into after 2026, to tell tenants the property may be in a flood hazard area, that the landlord's insurance does not cover tenants' belongings, and where to find county flood-risk information.

wa:SB 6246.title: Concerning emissions from emissions-intensive, trade-exposed facilities under the climate commitment act.
wa:SB 6246.summary: Fixes the industry classification codes for emissions-intensive, trade-exposed facilities under the cap-and-invest program as of January 1, 2026, and requires Ecology to recommend by December 1, 2026 how to schedule free allowance reductions for 2035-2050.

wa:SB 6260.title: Implementing efficiencies and programming changes in public education.
wa:SB 6260.summary: Changes school funding rules: minimum bus lifetimes of 10 years (category A) and 15 years (C and D) for depreciation payments, reduced reimbursement for zero-emission buses, and Running Start funded enrollment capped at 1.2 or 1.3 FTEs instead of 1.4.

wa:SB 6302.title: Concerning misclassification in the finishing trades on public works projects.
wa:SB 6302.summary: Requires Labor and Industries to investigate possible misclassification when a contractor uses three or more independent contractors for drywall, flooring, tiling, painting or glazing work on a public works project, on referral by the owner, contractors, unions or workers.

wa:SB 6309.title: Providing for enhanced municipal permitting tools for high capacity transit projects.
wa:SB 6309.summary: Lets regional transit authorities apply for permits before acquiring property or before local land use decisions, with notice to owners, and build light rail guideway facilities exceeding local height and setback limits where practicable.

wa:SB 6346.title: Establishing a tax on millionaires.
wa:SB 6346.summary: Amendment adding an exemption for income derived by small forestland owners from the income tax imposed by the bill.

wa:SB 6355.title: Concerning the electric transmission system.
wa:SB 6355.summary: Creates the Washington Electric Transmission Authority, a public body that works to expand electric transmission capacity, pursue upgrades to existing lines, and partner with utilities, tribes and neighboring states on transmission projects.
